Do not insult what other people worship
Own your choices instead of blaming Allah's decree or others
Make faith show up in deeds now rather than waiting
Memorize and regularly make the dua of Adam in 7:23

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

2:124.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتࣲ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّۖ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامࣰ اۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِيۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهۡدِي ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:124.en: And (remember) when his Lord tried Abraham with (His) commands, and he fulfilled them, He said: Lo! I have appointed thee a leader for mankind. (Abraham) said: And of my offspring (will there be leaders)? He said: My covenant includeth not wrong-doers

10:14.ar: ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ خَلَٰٓئِفَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ لِنَنظُرَ كَيۡفَ تَعۡمَلُونَ
10:14.en: Then We appointed you viceroys in the earth after them, that We might see how ye behave

5:105.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ لَا يَضُرُّكُم مَّن ضَلَّ إِذَا ٱهۡتَدَيۡتُمۡۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
5:105.en: O ye who believe! Ye have charge of your own souls. He who erreth cannot injure you if ye are rightly guided. Unto Allah ye will all return; and then He will inform you of what ye used to do

21:23.ar: لَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفۡعَلُ وَهُمۡ يُسۡـَٔلُونَ
21:23.en: He will not be questioned as to that which He doeth, but they will be questioned

38:26.ar: يَٰدَاوُۥدُ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَٰكَ خَلِيفَةࣰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱحۡكُم بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ ٱلۡهَوَىٰ فَيُضِلَّكَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدُۢ بِمَا نَسُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
38:26.en: (And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a viceroy in the earth; therefor judge aright between mankind, and follow not desire that it beguile thee from the way of Allah. Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning

CGU1iqBpiBQ.speaker: adnan
CGU1iqBpiBQ.speaker_note: continues his own Ramadan values series, referring back to the previous night's lesson
CGU1iqBpiBQ.title: The Values of Islam: Mas'uliyyah and Istikhlaf (Responsibility and Stewardship)
CGU1iqBpiBQ.one_line: Humans are stewards, not owners: with unique power comes answerability for oneself, family, community, creatures and the earth, and the opposite is indifference.
CGU1iqBpiBQ.summary: The sheikh pairs responsibility, which looks both back and forward, with stewardship, a forward-looking care that depends on it. Moral maturity, which we demand of children, means seeing what we hold as entrusted rather than owned, and adults forget to apply it to their homes, families and jobs. Humanity's place in the ecosystem is unique: unlike animals that adapt, humans reshape their environment, so power brings obligation and answerability, whether for climate change or for artificial intelligence, which needs stewards more than more intelligence. He grounds this in Allah appointing a khalifah on earth, Ibrahim made an imam, nations made successors to be tested, and the hadith that each of us is a shepherd who will be questioned. The hadith of planting a sapling as the Hour arrives shows that one does one's part however small. Responsibility starts with oneself but does not end there: Abu Bakr corrected those misusing the verse about minding oneself, and the ship parable shows we sail or sink together. Responsibility then widens with ability, from self to family, business and community. Its opposite is indifference. Dawud, who held nearly every human role, was the Quran's model khalifah, and Umar feared being asked about a stumbling animal. Children must be raised as caregivers.

outline.heading: Two values central to the prophets' message
outline.gist: Responsibility and stewardship may not hold the same centrality in other world religions.

outline.heading: Responsibility comes first
outline.gist: One can be responsible without being a steward, but stewardship cannot exist without responsibility.

outline.heading: Looking back and looking forward
outline.gist: Responsibility covers past acts and future duties, while stewardship looks forward; philosophers see both as the burden of being a self.

outline.heading: From mine to entrusted
outline.gist: We teach children that their toy is entrusted to them but forget that our homes, families and jobs are also trusts from Allah.

outline.heading: Power without stewardship
outline.gist: Power without responsibility is volatile; the world needs stewards of intelligence more than artificial intelligence.

outline.heading: What are we in the ecosystem?
outline.gist: Every creature fits its place; humans must ask whether they are members, masters or managers.

outline.heading: With power comes obligation
outline.gist: Free will and intelligence oblige humans to use their power responsibly.

outline.heading: Changing the environment and answering for it
outline.gist: Animals adapt over millions of years while humans reshape their surroundings, perhaps too much, and will be asked about it.

outline.heading: A khalifah on earth
outline.gist: Right after the opening of Al-Baqarah, Allah declares a steward on earth; earth, not Paradise, was always the plan.

outline.heading: Ibrahim made an imam
outline.gist: A steward is responsible for others' wellbeing on behalf of Someone else; what he holds is not his.

outline.heading: Successors so Allah sees how you act
outline.gist: Nations are made successors to be tested on what they do with their power.

outline.heading: Each of you is a shepherd
outline.gist: Ra'i means caregiver: the man at home, the woman in her house, the leader of his people, all will be questioned.

outline.heading: Plant the sapling as the Hour comes
outline.gist: Do your part however small, within the reach you have been given.

outline.heading: It starts with yourself, but does not end there
outline.gist: Some took the verse on minding oneself to mean no responsibility for others; Abu Bakr corrected that reading.

outline.heading: The ship: sail together or sink together
outline.gist: Those on the lower deck drilling a hole sink everyone unless others stop them.

outline.heading: We would rather not be responsible
outline.gist: People accept responsibility for themselves only to keep their freedom; Allah alone is not questioned, and this job description gives a Muslim his meaning.

outline.heading: The widening wingspan
outline.gist: Care grows from self to siblings, spouse, children, extended family, employees and community as Allah grants more.

outline.heading: The opposite is indifference
outline.gist: The first time the companions heard 'khalifah', they learned that 'not my problem' does not work.

outline.heading: Good and bad not caring
outline.gist: Not caring about people's opinions is admirable; not caring about moral responsibility is not.

outline.heading: Dawud, the model steward
outline.gist: Prophet, king, commander, craftsman, singer of the Zabur, judge, husband and father: he held the widest span of roles.

outline.heading: Caregivers of earth and creatures
outline.gist: Animals cannot make laws to avoid extinction; humans can protect them or destroy them and each other.

outline.heading: Umar and the stumbling animal
outline.gist: People in power today lack stewardship; Umar lay awake fearing he would be asked about an unpaved road.

outline.heading: Raising children as caregivers
outline.gist: Children must grow up knowing they are responsible for everything entrusted to them.

themes.note: Humans hold everything as a trust from Allah and will be questioned about it.

themes.label: Agency, responsibility and rejecting victim mentality
themes.note: People avoid responsibility though it is the job description that gives life meaning.

themes.label: Environment and stewardship of the earth
themes.note: Humans reshape the environment and are answerable for the damage.

themes.label: Technology, AI, social media and attention
themes.note: AI needs responsible stewards more than more intelligence.

themes.label: Commanding good and forbidding wrong (amr bil-ma'ruf)
themes.note: Abu Bakr's correction and the ship parable: responsibility for the wrongs around you.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Being a caregiver is the Muslim's ready-made meaning.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Dawud and Umar as models of power joined with stewardship.

themes.label: Parenting and raising children
themes.note: Moral maturity in children as moving from 'mine' to 'entrusted'.

quran.point: I will place a khalifah on earth.
Ibrahim made an imam for people.
Made successors on earth after them to see how you would act.
Upon you is yourselves; those astray cannot harm you if you are guided, misused to deny responsibility.
Allah is not questioned about what He does, but they will be.

hadith.gist: Each of you is a shepherd and each is responsible for his flock: the man in his house, the woman in her home, the leader over his people.
If the Hour comes while one of you holds a sapling, let him plant it if he can.
Abu Bakr said people misuse the verse 'upon you is yourselves'; he heard the Prophet say that if people see wrong and do not change it, Allah's punishment is near.
Parable of the ship: those on the lower deck drill a hole for water; if the others stop them all are saved, if not all drown.

Power without stewardship is volatility
We sail together or sink together
Responsibility works in both directions
The opposite is indifference

11:1.ar: الٓرۚ كِتَٰبٌ أُحۡكِمَتۡ ءَايَٰتُهُۥ ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتۡ مِن لَّدُنۡ حَكِيمٍ خَبِيرٍ
11:1.en: Alif. Lam. Ra. (This is) a Scripture the revelations whereof are perfected and then expounded. (It cometh) from One Wise, Informed

11:2.ar: أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّنِي لَكُم مِّنۡهُ نَذِيرࣱ وَبَشِيرࣱ‏
11:2.en: (Saying): Serve none but Allah. Lo! I am unto you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings

11:3.ar: وَأَنِ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِ يُمَتِّعۡكُم مَّتَٰعًا حَسَنًا إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ى وَيُؤۡتِ كُلَّ ذِي فَضۡلࣲ فَضۡلَهُۥۖ وَإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ عَذَابَ يَوۡمࣲ كَبِيرٍ
11:3.en: And (bidding you): Ask pardon of your Lord and turn to Him repentant. He will cause you to enjoy a fair estate until a time appointed. He giveth His bounty unto every bountiful one. But if ye turn away, lo! (then) I fear for you the retribution of an awful Day

11:4.ar: إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
11:4.en: Unto Allah is your return, and He is Able to do all things

11:5.ar: أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ يَثۡنُونَ صُدُورَهُمۡ لِيَسۡتَخۡفُواْ مِنۡهُۚ أَلَا حِينَ يَسۡتَغۡشُونَ ثِيَابَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعۡلِنُونَۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
11:5.en: Lo! now they fold up their breasts that they may hide (their thoughts) from Him. At the very moment when they cover themselves with their clothing, Allah knoweth that which they keep hidden and that which they proclaim. Lo! He is Aware of what is in the breasts (of men)

11:6.ar: ۞وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رِزۡقُهَا وَيَعۡلَمُ مُسۡتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسۡتَوۡدَعَهَاۚ كُلࣱّ فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
11:6.en: And there is not a beast in the earth but the sustenance thereof dependeth on Allah. He knoweth its habitation and its repository. All is in a clear Record

11:7.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ وَكَانَ عَرۡشُهُۥ عَلَى ٱلۡمَآءِ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلࣰ اۗ وَلَئِن قُلۡتَ إِنَّكُم مَّبۡعُوثُونَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ لَيَقُولَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحۡرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
11:7.en: And He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days - and His Throne was upon the water - that He might try you, which of you is best in conduct. Yet if thou (O Muhammad) sayest: Lo! ye will be raised again after death! those who disbelieve will surely say: This is naught but mere magic

11:8.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَخَّرۡنَا عَنۡهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمَّةࣲ مَّعۡدُودَةࣲ لَّيَقُولُنَّ مَا يَحۡبِسُهُۥٓۗ أَلَا يَوۡمَ يَأۡتِيهِمۡ لَيۡسَ مَصۡرُوفًا عَنۡهُمۡ وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
11:8.en: And if We delay for them the doom until a reckoned time, they will surely say: What withholdeth it? Verily on the day when it cometh unto them, it cannot be averted from them, and that which they derided will surround them

11:9.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَذَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِنَّا رَحۡمَةࣰ ثُمَّ نَزَعۡنَٰهَا مِنۡهُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيَـُٔوسࣱ كَفُورࣱ‏
11:9.en: And if we cause man to taste some mercy from Us and afterward withdraw it from him, lo! he is despairing, thankless

11:10.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَذَقۡنَٰهُ نَعۡمَآءَ بَعۡدَ ضَرَّآءَ مَسَّتۡهُ لَيَقُولَنَّ ذَهَبَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتُ عَنِّيٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَفَرِحࣱ فَخُورٌ
11:10.en: And if We cause him to taste grace after some misfortune that had befallen him, he saith: The ills have gone from me. Lo! he is exultant, boastful

11:11.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
11:11.en: Save those who persevere and do good works. Theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward

11:12.ar: فَلَعَلَّكَ تَارِكُۢ بَعۡضَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكَ وَضَآئِقُۢ بِهِۦ صَدۡرُكَ أَن يَقُولُواْ لَوۡلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيۡهِ كَنزٌ أَوۡ جَآءَ مَعَهُۥ مَلَكٌۚ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ نَذِيرࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَكِيلٌ
11:12.en: A likely thing, that thou wouldst forsake aught of that which hath been revealed unto thee, and that thy breast should be straitened for it, because they say: Why hath not a treasure been sent down for him, or an angel come with him? Thou art but a warner, and Allah is in charge of all things

11:13.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ ٱفۡتَرَىٰهُۖ قُلۡ فَأۡتُواْ بِعَشۡرِ سُوَرࣲ مِّثۡلِهِۦ مُفۡتَرَيَٰتࣲ وَٱدۡعُواْ مَنِ ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
11:13.en: Or they say: He hath invented it. Say: Then bring ten surahs, the like thereof, invented, and call on everyone ye can beside Allah, if ye are truthful

11:14.ar: فَإِلَّمۡ يَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لَكُمۡ فَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ بِعِلۡمِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ فَهَلۡ أَنتُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ
11:14.en: And if they answer not your prayer, then know that it is revealed only in the knowledge of Allah; and that there is no Allah save Him. Will ye then be (of) those who surrender

11:15.ar: مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتَهَا نُوَفِّ إِلَيۡهِمۡ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ فِيهَا وَهُمۡ فِيهَا لَا يُبۡخَسُونَ
11:15.en: Whoso desireth the life of the world and its pomp, We shall repay them their deeds herein, and therein they will not be wronged

11:16.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَيۡسَ لَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِلَّا ٱلنَّارُۖ وَحَبِطَ مَا صَنَعُواْ فِيهَا وَبَٰطِلࣱ مَّا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
11:16.en: Those are they for whom is naught in the Hereafter save the Fire. (All) that they contrive here is vain and (all) that they are wont to do is fruitless

11:17.ar: أَفَمَن كَانَ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ وَيَتۡلُوهُ شَاهِدࣱ مِّنۡهُ وَمِن قَبۡلِهِۦ كِتَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِمَامࣰ ا وَرَحۡمَةًۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِهِۦۚ وَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابِ فَٱلنَّارُ مَوۡعِدُهُۥۚ فَلَا تَكُ فِي مِرۡيَةࣲ مِّنۡهُۚ إِنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
11:17.en: Is he (to be counted equal with them) who relieth on a clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him reciteth it, and before it was the Book of Moses, an example and a mercy? Such believe therein, and whoso disbelieveth therein of the clans, the Fire is his appointed place. So be not thou in doubt concerning it. Lo! it is the Truth from thy Lord; but most of mankind believe not

11:18.ar: وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًاۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُعۡرَضُونَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ وَيَقُولُ ٱلۡأَشۡهَٰدُ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَبُواْ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡۚ أَلَا لَعۡنَةُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
11:18.en: Who doeth greater wrong than he who inventeth a lie concerning Allah? Such will be brought before their Lord, and the witnesses will say: These are they who lied concerning their Lord. Now the curse of Allah is upon wrong-doers

11:19.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَبۡغُونَهَا عِوَجࣰ ا وَهُم بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ كَٰفِرُونَ
11:19.en: Who debar (men) from the way of Allah and would have it crooked, and who are disbelievers in the Hereafter

11:20.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَمۡ يَكُونُواْ مُعۡجِزِينَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا كَانَ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِنۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَۘ يُضَٰعَفُ لَهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُۚ مَا كَانُواْ يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَمَا كَانُواْ يُبۡصِرُونَ
11:20.en: Such will not escape in the earth, nor have they any protecting friends beside Allah. For them the torment will be double. They could not bear to hear, and they used not to see

11:21.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَضَلَّ عَنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ
11:21.en: Such are they who have lost their souls, and that which they used to invent hath failed them

11:22.ar: لَا جَرَمَ أَنَّهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمُ ٱلۡأَخۡسَرُونَ
11:22.en: Assuredly in the Hereafter they will be the greatest losers

11:23.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَأَخۡبَتُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
11:23.en: Lo! those who believe and do good works and humble themselves before their Lord: such are rightful owners of the Garden; they will abide therein

11:24.ar: ۞مَثَلُ ٱلۡفَرِيقَيۡنِ كَٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ وَٱلۡأَصَمِّ وَٱلۡبَصِيرِ وَٱلسَّمِيعِۚ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِيَانِ مَثَلًاۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
11:24.en: The similitude of the two parties is as the blind and the deaf and the seer and the hearer. Are they equal in similitude? Will ye not then be admonished

11:25.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنِّي لَكُمۡ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينٌ
11:25.en: And We sent Noah unto his folk (and he said): Lo! I am a plain warner unto you

11:26.ar: أَن لَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ عَذَابَ يَوۡمٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
11:26.en: That ye serve none, save Allah. Lo! I fear for you the retribution of a painful Day

11:27.ar: فَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا مِّثۡلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِيَ ٱلرَّأۡيِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمۡ عَلَيۡنَا مِن فَضۡلِۭ بَلۡ نَظُنُّكُمۡ كَٰذِبِينَ
11:27.en: The chieftains of his folk, who disbelieved, said: We see thee but a mortal like us, and we see not that any follow thee save the most abject among us, without reflection. We behold in you no merit above us - nay, we deem you liars

11:28.ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّي وَءَاتَىٰنِي رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِهِۦ فَعُمِّيَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنُلۡزِمُكُمُوهَا وَأَنتُمۡ لَهَا كَٰرِهُونَ
11:28.en: He said: O my people! Bethink you, if I rely on a clear proof from my Lord and there hath come unto me a mercy from His presence, and it hath been made obscure to you, can we compel you to accept it when ye are averse thereto

11:29.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ لَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مَالًاۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِطَارِدِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَٰكِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا تَجۡهَلُونَ
11:29.en: And O my people! I ask of you no wealth therefor. My reward is the concern only of Allah, and I am not going to thrust away those who believe - Lo! they have to meet their Lord! - but I see you a folk that are ignorant

11:30.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ مَن يَنصُرُنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِن طَرَدتُّهُمۡۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
11:30.en: And, O my people! who would deliver me from Allah if I thrust them away? Will ye not then reflect

11:31.ar: وَلَآ أَقُولُ لَكُمۡ عِندِي خَزَآئِنُ ٱللَّهِ وَلَآ أَعۡلَمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ وَلَآ أَقُولُ إِنِّي مَلَكࣱ وَلَآ أَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ تَزۡدَرِيٓ أَعۡيُنُكُمۡ لَن يُؤۡتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ خَيۡرًاۖ ٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ إِنِّيٓ إِذࣰ ا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
11:31.en: I say not unto you: "I have the treasures of Allah" nor "I have knowledge of the Unseen," nor say I: "Lo! I am an angel!" Nor say I unto those whom your eyes scorn that Allah will not give them good - Allah knoweth best what is in their hearts - Lo! then indeed I should be of the wrong-doers

11:32.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰنُوحُ قَدۡ جَٰدَلۡتَنَا فَأَكۡثَرۡتَ جِدَٰلَنَا فَأۡتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
11:32.en: They said: O Noah! Thou hast disputed with us and multiplied disputation with us; now bring upon us that wherewith thou threatenest us, if thou art of the truthful

11:33.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَأۡتِيكُم بِهِ ٱللَّهُ إِن شَآءَ وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُعۡجِزِينَ
11:33.en: He said: Only Allah will bring it upon you if He will, and ye can by no means escape

11:34.ar: وَلَا يَنفَعُكُمۡ نُصۡحِيٓ إِنۡ أَرَدتُّ أَنۡ أَنصَحَ لَكُمۡ إِن كَانَ ٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَن يُغۡوِيَكُمۡۚ هُوَ رَبُّكُمۡ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
11:34.en: My counsel will not profit you if I were minded to advise you, if Allah's will is to keep you astray. He is your Lord and unto Him ye will be brought back

11:35.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ ٱفۡتَرَىٰهُۖ قُلۡ إِنِ ٱفۡتَرَيۡتُهُۥ فَعَلَيَّ إِجۡرَامِي وَأَنَا۠ بَرِيٓءࣱ مِّمَّا تُجۡرِمُونَ
11:35.en: Or say they (again): He hath invented it? Say: If I have invented it, upon me be my crimes, but I am innocent of (all) that ye commit

11:36.ar: وَأُوحِيَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُۥ لَن يُؤۡمِنَ مِن قَوۡمِكَ إِلَّا مَن قَدۡ ءَامَنَ فَلَا تَبۡتَئِسۡ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
11:36.en: And it was inspired in Noah, (saying): No-one of thy folk will believe save him who hath believed already. Be not distressed because of what they do

11:37.ar: وَٱصۡنَعِ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَا وَوَحۡيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبۡنِي فِي ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِنَّهُم مُّغۡرَقُونَ
11:37.en: Build the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and speak not unto Me on behalf of those who do wrong. Lo! they will be drowned

11:38.ar: وَيَصۡنَعُ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيۡهِ مَلَأࣱ مِّن قَوۡمِهِۦ سَخِرُواْ مِنۡهُۚ قَالَ إِن تَسۡخَرُواْ مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسۡخَرُ مِنكُمۡ كَمَا تَسۡخَرُونَ
11:38.en: And he was building the ship, and every time that chieftains of his people passed him, they made mock of him. He said: Though ye make mock of Us, yet We mock at you even as ye mock

11:39.ar: فَسَوۡفَ تَعۡلَمُونَ مَن يَأۡتِيهِ عَذَابࣱ يُخۡزِيهِ وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيۡهِ عَذَابࣱ مُّقِيمٌ
11:39.en: And ye shall know to whom a punishment that will confound him cometh, and upon whom a lasting doom will fall

11:40.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمۡرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلۡنَا ٱحۡمِلۡ فِيهَا مِن كُلࣲّ زَوۡجَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ وَأَهۡلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ وَمَنۡ ءَامَنَۚ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱ‏
11:40.en: (Thus it was) till, when Our commandment came to pass and the oven gushed forth water, We said: Load therein two of every kind, a pair (the male and female), and thy household, save him against whom the word hath gone forth already, and those who believe. And but a few were they who believed with him

11:41.ar: ۞وَقَالَ ٱرۡكَبُواْ فِيهَا بِسۡمِ ٱللَّهِ مَجۡرٜىٰهَا وَمُرۡسَىٰهَآۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَغَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
11:41.en: And he said: Embark therein! In the name of Allah be its course and its mooring. Lo! my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful

11:42.ar: وَهِيَ تَجۡرِي بِهِمۡ فِي مَوۡجࣲ كَٱلۡجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبۡنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِي مَعۡزِلࣲ يَٰبُنَيَّ ٱرۡكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
11:42.en: And it sailed with them amid waves like mountains, and Noah cried unto his son - and he was standing aloof - O my son! Come ride with us, and be not with the disbelievers

11:43.ar: قَالَ سَـَٔاوِيٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلࣲ يَعۡصِمُنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِۚ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَۚ وَحَالَ بَيۡنَهُمَا ٱلۡمَوۡجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُغۡرَقِينَ
11:43.en: He said: I shall betake me to some mountain that will save me from the water. (Noah) said: This day there is none that saveth from the commandment of Allah save him on whom He hath had mercy. And the wave came in between them, so he was among the drowned

11:44.ar: وَقِيلَ يَٰٓأَرۡضُ ٱبۡلَعِي مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقۡلِعِي وَغِيضَ ٱلۡمَآءُ وَقُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ وَٱسۡتَوَتۡ عَلَى ٱلۡجُودِيِّۖ وَقِيلَ بُعۡدࣰ ا لِّلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
11:44.en: And it was said: O earth! Swallow thy water and, O sky! be cleared of clouds! And the water was made to subside. And the commandment was fulfilled. And it (the ship) came to rest upon (the mount) Al-Judi and it was said: A far removal for wrongdoing folk

11:45.ar: وَنَادَىٰ نُوحࣱ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبۡنِي مِنۡ أَهۡلِي وَإِنَّ وَعۡدَكَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحۡكَمُ ٱلۡحَٰكِمِينَ
11:45.en: And Noah cried unto his Lord and said: My Lord! Lo! my son is of my household! Surely Thy promise is the truth and Thou are the Most Just of Judges

11:46.ar: قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيۡسَ مِنۡ أَهۡلِكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيۡرُ صَٰلِحࣲۖ فَلَا تَسۡـَٔلۡنِ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۖ إِنِّيٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
11:46.en: He said: O Noah! Lo! he is not of thy household; lo! he is of evil conduct, so ask not of Me that whereof thou hast no knowledge. I admonish thee lest thou be among the ignorant

11:47.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّيٓ أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنۡ أَسۡـَٔلَكَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱۖ وَإِلَّا تَغۡفِرۡ لِي وَتَرۡحَمۡنِيٓ أَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
11:47.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! in Thee do I seek refuge (from the sin) that I should ask of Thee that whereof I have no knowledge. Unless Thou forgive me and have mercy on me I shall be among the lost

11:48.ar: قِيلَ يَٰنُوحُ ٱهۡبِطۡ بِسَلَٰمࣲ مِّنَّا وَبَرَكَٰتٍ عَلَيۡكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ أُمَمࣲ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَۚ وَأُمَمࣱ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمۡ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
11:48.en: It was said (unto him): O Noah! Go thou down (from the mountain) with peace from Us and blessings upon thee and some nations (that will spring) from those with thee. (There will be other) nations unto whom We shall give enjoyment a long while and then a painful doom from Us will overtake them

11:49.ar: تِلۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ نُوحِيهَآ إِلَيۡكَۖ مَا كُنتَ تَعۡلَمُهَآ أَنتَ وَلَا قَوۡمُكَ مِن قَبۡلِ هَٰذَاۖ فَٱصۡبِرۡۖ إِنَّ ٱلۡعَٰقِبَةَ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
11:49.en: This is of the tidings of the Unseen which We inspire in thee (Muhammad). Thou thyself knewest it not, nor did thy folk (know it) before this. Then have patience. Lo! the sequel is for those who ward off (evil)

11:50.ar: وَإِلَىٰ عَادٍ أَخَاهُمۡ هُودࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥٓۖ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا مُفۡتَرُونَ
11:50.en: And unto (the tribe of) A'ad (We sent) their brother, Hud. He said: O my people! Serve Allah! Ye have no other Allah save Him. Lo! ye do but invent

11:51.ar: يَٰقَوۡمِ لَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ أَجۡرًاۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِيٓۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
11:51.en: O my people! I ask of you no reward for it. Lo! my reward is the concern only of Him Who made me. Have ye then no sense

11:52.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِ يُرۡسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّدۡرَارࣰ ا وَيَزِدۡكُمۡ قُوَّةً إِلَىٰ قُوَّتِكُمۡ وَلَا تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ مُجۡرِمِينَ
11:52.en: And, O my people! Ask forgiveness of your Lord, then turn unto Him repentant; He will cause the sky to rain abundance on you and will add unto you strength to your strength. Turn not away, guilty

11:53.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰهُودُ مَا جِئۡتَنَا بِبَيِّنَةࣲ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِتَارِكِيٓ ءَالِهَتِنَا عَن قَوۡلِكَ وَمَا نَحۡنُ لَكَ بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
11:53.en: They said: O Hud! Thou hast brought us no clear proof and we are not going to forsake our gods on thy (mere) saying, and we are not believers in thee

11:54.ar: إِن نَّقُولُ إِلَّا ٱعۡتَرَىٰكَ بَعۡضُ ءَالِهَتِنَا بِسُوٓءࣲۗ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أُشۡهِدُ ٱللَّهَ وَٱشۡهَدُوٓاْ أَنِّي بَرِيٓءࣱ مِّمَّا تُشۡرِكُونَ
11:54.en: We say naught save that one of our gods hath possessed thee in an evil way. He said: I call Allah to witness, and do ye (too) bear witness, that I am innocent of (all) that ye ascribe as partners (to Allah)

11:55.ar: مِن دُونِهِۦۖ فَكِيدُونِي جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ لَا تُنظِرُونِ
11:55.en: Beside Him. So (try to) circumvent me, all of you, give me no respite

11:56.ar: إِنِّي تَوَكَّلۡتُ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمۚ مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذُۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
11:56.en: Lo! I have put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Not an animal but He doth grasp it by the forelock! Lo! my Lord is on a straight path

11:57.ar: فَإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَقَدۡ أَبۡلَغۡتُكُم مَّآ أُرۡسِلۡتُ بِهِۦٓ إِلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَيَسۡتَخۡلِفُ رَبِّي قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ وَلَا تَضُرُّونَهُۥ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٍ حَفِيظࣱ‏
11:57.en: And if ye turn away, still I have conveyed unto you that wherewith I was sent unto you, and my Lord will set in place of you a folk other than you. Ye cannot injure Him at all. Lo! my Lord is Guardian over all things

11:58.ar: وَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمۡرُنَا نَجَّيۡنَا هُودࣰ ا وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ بِرَحۡمَةࣲ مِّنَّا وَنَجَّيۡنَٰهُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظࣲ‏
11:58.en: And when Our commandment came to pass We saved Hud and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us; We saved them from a harsh doom

11:59.ar: وَتِلۡكَ عَادࣱۖ جَحَدُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَعَصَوۡاْ رُسُلَهُۥ وَٱتَّبَعُوٓاْ أَمۡرَ كُلِّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدࣲ‏
11:59.en: And such were A'ad. They denied the revelations of their Lord and flouted His messengers and followed the command of every froward potentate

11:60.ar: وَأُتۡبِعُواْ فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعۡنَةࣰ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ عَادࣰ ا كَفَرُواْ رَبَّهُمۡۗ أَلَا بُعۡدࣰ ا لِّعَادࣲ قَوۡمِ هُودࣲ‏
11:60.en: And a curse was made to follow them in the world and on the Day of Resurrection. Lo! A'ad disbelieved in their Lord. A far removal for A'ad, the folk of Hud

11:61.ar: ۞وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمۡ صَٰلِحࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥۖ هُوَ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱسۡتَعۡمَرَكُمۡ فِيهَا فَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُوهُ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي قَرِيبࣱ مُّجِيبࣱ‏
11:61.en: And unto (the tribe of) Thamud (We sent) their brother Salih. He said: O my people! Serve Allah, Ye have no other Allah save Him. He brought you forth from the earth and hath made you husband it. So ask forgiveness of Him and turn unto Him repentant. Lo! my Lord is Nigh, Responsive

11:62.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰصَٰلِحُ قَدۡ كُنتَ فِينَا مَرۡجُوࣰّ ا قَبۡلَ هَٰذَآۖ أَتَنۡهَىٰنَآ أَن نَّعۡبُدَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَا وَإِنَّنَا لَفِي شَكࣲّ مِّمَّا تَدۡعُونَآ إِلَيۡهِ مُرِيبࣲ‏
11:62.en: They said: O Salih! Thou hast been among us hitherto as that wherein our hope was placed. Dost thou ask us not to worship what our fathers worshipped? Lo! we verily are in grave doubt concerning that to which thou callest us

11:63.ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّي وَءَاتَىٰنِي مِنۡهُ رَحۡمَةࣰ فَمَن يَنصُرُنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِنۡ عَصَيۡتُهُۥۖ فَمَا تَزِيدُونَنِي غَيۡرَ تَخۡسِيرࣲ‏
11:63.en: He said: O my people! Bethink you: if I am (acting) on clear proof from my Lord and there hath come unto me a mercy from Him, who will save me from Allah if I disobey Him? Ye would add to me naught save perdition

11:64.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ هَٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمۡ ءَايَةࣰۖ فَذَرُوهَا تَأۡكُلۡ فِيٓ أَرۡضِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوٓءࣲ فَيَأۡخُذَكُمۡ عَذَابࣱ قَرِيبࣱ‏
11:64.en: O my people! This is the camel of Allah, a token unto you, so suffer her to feed in Allah's earth, and touch her not with harm lest a near torment seize you

11:65.ar: فَعَقَرُوهَا فَقَالَ تَمَتَّعُواْ فِي دَارِكُمۡ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامࣲۖ ذَٰلِكَ وَعۡدٌ غَيۡرُ مَكۡذُوبࣲ‏
11:65.en: But they hamstrung her, and then he said: Enjoy life in your dwelling-place three days! This is a threat that will not be belied

11:66.ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمۡرُنَا نَجَّيۡنَا صَٰلِحࣰ ا وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ بِرَحۡمَةࣲ مِّنَّا وَمِنۡ خِزۡيِ يَوۡمِئِذٍۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ ٱلۡقَوِيُّ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ
11:66.en: So, when Our commandment came to pass, We saved Salih, and those who believed with him, by a mercy from Us, from the ignominy of that day. Lo, thy Lord! He is the Strong, the Mighty

11:67.ar: وَأَخَذَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ ٱلصَّيۡحَةُ فَأَصۡبَحُواْ فِي دِيَٰرِهِمۡ جَٰثِمِينَ
11:67.en: And the (awful) Cry overtook those who did wrong, so that morning found them prostrate in their dwellings

11:68.ar: كَأَن لَّمۡ يَغۡنَوۡاْ فِيهَآۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ ثَمُودَاْ كَفَرُواْ رَبَّهُمۡۗ أَلَا بُعۡدࣰ ا لِّثَمُودَ
11:68.en: As though they had not dwelt there. Lo! Thamud disbelieved in their Lord. A far removal for Thamud

11:69.ar: وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡ رُسُلُنَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ بِٱلۡبُشۡرَىٰ قَالُواْ سَلَٰمࣰ اۖ قَالَ سَلَٰمࣱۖ فَمَا لَبِثَ أَن جَآءَ بِعِجۡلٍ حَنِيذࣲ‏
11:69.en: And Our messengers cam unto Abraham with good news. They said: Peace! He answered: Peace! and delayed not to bring a roasted calf

11:70.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَآ أَيۡدِيَهُمۡ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيۡهِ نَكِرَهُمۡ وَأَوۡجَسَ مِنۡهُمۡ خِيفَةࣰۚ قَالُواْ لَا تَخَفۡ إِنَّآ أُرۡسِلۡنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِ لُوطࣲ‏
11:70.en: And when he saw their hands reached not to it, he mistrusted them and conceived a fear of them. They said: Fear not! Lo! we are sent unto the folk of Lot

11:71.ar: وَٱمۡرَأَتُهُۥ قَآئِمَةࣱ فَضَحِكَتۡ فَبَشَّرۡنَٰهَا بِإِسۡحَٰقَ وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسۡحَٰقَ يَعۡقُوبَ
11:71.en: And his wife, standing by laughed when We gave her good tidings (of the birth) of Isaac, and, after Isaac, of Jacob

11:72.ar: قَالَتۡ يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰٓ ءَأَلِدُ وَأَنَا۠ عَجُوزࣱ وَهَٰذَا بَعۡلِي شَيۡخًاۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَيۡءٌ عَجِيبࣱ‏
11:72.en: She said: Oh woe is me! Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman, and this my husband is an old man? Lo! this is a strange thing

11:73.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أَتَعۡجَبِينَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِۖ رَحۡمَتُ ٱللَّهِ وَبَرَكَٰتُهُۥ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِۚ إِنَّهُۥ حَمِيدࣱ مَّجِيدࣱ‏
11:73.en: They said: Wonderest thou at the commandment of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house! Lo! He is Owner of Praise, Owner of Glory

11:74.ar: فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ ٱلرَّوۡعُ وَجَآءَتۡهُ ٱلۡبُشۡرَىٰ يُجَٰدِلُنَا فِي قَوۡمِ لُوطٍ
11:74.en: And when the awe departed from Abraham, and the glad news reached him, he pleaded with Us on behalf of the folk of Lot

11:75.en: Lo! Abraham was mild, imploring, penitent

11:76.ar: يَٰٓإِبۡرَٰهِيمُ أَعۡرِضۡ عَنۡ هَٰذَآۖ إِنَّهُۥ قَدۡ جَآءَ أَمۡرُ رَبِّكَۖ وَإِنَّهُمۡ ءَاتِيهِمۡ عَذَابٌ غَيۡرُ مَرۡدُودࣲ‏
11:76.en: (It was said) O Abraham! Forsake this! Lo! thy Lord's commandment hath gone forth, and lo! there cometh unto them a doom which cannot be repelled

11:77.ar: وَلَمَّا جَآءَتۡ رُسُلُنَا لُوطࣰ ا سِيٓءَ بِهِمۡ وَضَاقَ بِهِمۡ ذَرۡعࣰ ا وَقَالَ هَٰذَا يَوۡمٌ عَصِيبࣱ‏
11:77.en: And when Our messengers came unto Lot, he was distressed and knew not how to protect them. He said: This is a distressful day

11:78.ar: وَجَآءَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ يُهۡرَعُونَ إِلَيۡهِ وَمِن قَبۡلُ كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ بَنَاتِي هُنَّ أَطۡهَرُ لَكُمۡۖ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُخۡزُونِ فِي ضَيۡفِيٓۖ أَلَيۡسَ مِنكُمۡ رَجُلࣱ رَّشِيدࣱ‏
11:78.en: And his people came unto him, running towards him - and before then they used to commit abominations - He said: O my people! Here are my daughters! They are purer for you. Beware of Allah, and degrade me not in (the person of) my guests. Is there not among you any upright man

11:79.ar: قَالُواْ لَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَ مَا لَنَا فِي بَنَاتِكَ مِنۡ حَقࣲّ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَعۡلَمُ مَا نُرِيدُ
11:79.en: They said: Well thou knowest that we have no right to thy daughters, and well thou knowest what we want

11:80.ar: قَالَ لَوۡ أَنَّ لِي بِكُمۡ قُوَّةً أَوۡ ءَاوِيٓ إِلَىٰ رُكۡنࣲ شَدِيدࣲ‏
11:80.en: He said: Would that I had strength to resist you or had some strong support (among you)

11:81.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓاْ إِلَيۡكَۖ فَأَسۡرِ بِأَهۡلِكَ بِقِطۡعࣲ مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَلَا يَلۡتَفِتۡ مِنكُمۡ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمۡرَأَتَكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ مَوۡعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبۡحُۚ أَلَيۡسَ ٱلصُّبۡحُ بِقَرِيبࣲ‏
11:81.en: (The messengers) said: O Lot! Lo! we are messengers of thy Lord; they shall not reach thee. So travel with thy people in a part of the night, and let not one of you turn round - (all) save thy wife. Lo! that which smiteth them will smite her (also). Lo! their tryst is (for) the morning. Is not the morning nigh

11:82.ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمۡرُنَا جَعَلۡنَا عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا وَأَمۡطَرۡنَا عَلَيۡهَا حِجَارَةࣰ مِّن سِجِّيلࣲ مَّنضُودࣲ‏
11:82.en: So when Our commandment came to pass We overthrew (that township) and rained upon it stones of clay, one after another

11:83.ar: مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَۖ وَمَا هِيَ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ بِبَعِيدࣲ‏
11:83.en: Marked with fire in the providence of thy Lord (for the destruction of the wicked). And they are never far from the wrong-doers

11:84.ar: ۞وَإِلَىٰ مَدۡيَنَ أَخَاهُمۡ شُعَيۡبࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥۖ وَلَا تَنقُصُواْ ٱلۡمِكۡيَالَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَۖ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكُم بِخَيۡرࣲ وَإِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ عَذَابَ يَوۡمࣲ مُّحِيطࣲ‏
11:84.en: And unto Midian (We sent) their brother Shu'eyb. He said: O my people! Serve Allah. Ye have no other Allah save Him! And give not short measure and short weight. Lo! I see you well-to-do, and lo! I fear for you the doom of a besetting Day

11:85.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ أَوۡفُواْ ٱلۡمِكۡيَالَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ وَلَا تَبۡخَسُواْ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشۡيَآءَهُمۡ وَلَا تَعۡثَوۡاْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مُفۡسِدِينَ
11:85.en: O my people! Give full measure and full weight in justice, and wrong not people in respect of their goods. And do not evil in the earth, causing corruption

11:86.ar: بَقِيَّتُ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَۚ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ عَلَيۡكُم بِحَفِيظࣲ‏
11:86.en: That which Allah leaveth with you is better for you if ye are believers; and I am not a keeper over you

11:87.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰشُعَيۡبُ أَصَلَوٰتُكَ تَأۡمُرُكَ أَن نَّتۡرُكَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَآ أَوۡ أَن نَّفۡعَلَ فِيٓ أَمۡوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُاْۖ إِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ ٱلۡحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ
11:87.en: They said: O Shu'eyb! Doth thy way of prayer command thee that we should forsake that which our fathers (used to) worship, or that we (should leave off) doing what we will with our own property. Lo! thou art the mild, the guide to right behaviour

11:88.ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّي وَرَزَقَنِي مِنۡهُ رِزۡقًا حَسَنࣰ اۚ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أُخَالِفَكُمۡ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنۡهَىٰكُمۡ عَنۡهُۚ إِنۡ أُرِيدُ إِلَّا ٱلۡإِصۡلَٰحَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُۚ وَمَا تَوۡفِيقِيٓ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِۚ عَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡتُ وَإِلَيۡهِ أُنِيبُ
11:88.en: He said: O my people! Bethink you: if I am (acting) on a clear proof from my Lord and He sustaineth me with fair sustenance from Him (how can I concede aught to you)? I desire not to do behind your backs that which I ask you not to do. I desire naught save reform so far as I am able. My welfare is only in Allah. In Him I trust and unto Him I turn (repentant)

11:89.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ لَا يَجۡرِمَنَّكُمۡ شِقَاقِيٓ أَن يُصِيبَكُم مِّثۡلُ مَآ أَصَابَ قَوۡمَ نُوحٍ أَوۡ قَوۡمَ هُودٍ أَوۡ قَوۡمَ صَٰلِحࣲۚ وَمَا قَوۡمُ لُوطࣲ مِّنكُم بِبَعِيدࣲ‏
11:89.en: And, O my people! Let not the schism with me cause you to sin so that there befall you that which befell the folk of Noah and the folk of Hud, and the folk of Salih; and the folk of Lot are not far off from you

11:90.ar: وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي رَحِيمࣱ وَدُودࣱ‏
11:90.en: Ask pardon of your Lord and then turn unto Him (repentant). Lo! my Lord is Merciful, Loving

11:91.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰشُعَيۡبُ مَا نَفۡقَهُ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّمَّا تَقُولُ وَإِنَّا لَنَرَىٰكَ فِينَا ضَعِيفࣰ اۖ وَلَوۡلَا رَهۡطُكَ لَرَجَمۡنَٰكَۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيۡنَا بِعَزِيزࣲ‏
11:91.en: They said: O Shu'eyb! We understand not much of that thou tellest, and lo! we do behold thee weak among us. But for thy family, we should have stoned thee, for thou art not strong against us

11:92.ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَرَهۡطِيٓ أَعَزُّ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱتَّخَذۡتُمُوهُ وَرَآءَكُمۡ ظِهۡرِيًّاۖ إِنَّ رَبِّي بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ مُحِيطࣱ‏
11:92.en: He said: O my people! Is my family more to be honoured by you than Allah? and ye put Him behind you, neglected! Lo! my Lord surroundeth what ye do

11:93.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡمَلُواْ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُمۡ إِنِّي عَٰمِلࣱۖ سَوۡفَ تَعۡلَمُونَ مَن يَأۡتِيهِ عَذَابࣱ يُخۡزِيهِ وَمَنۡ هُوَ كَٰذِبࣱۖ وَٱرۡتَقِبُوٓاْ إِنِّي مَعَكُمۡ رَقِيبࣱ‏
11:93.en: And, O my people! Act according to your power, lo! I (too) am acting. Ye will soon know on whom there cometh a doom that will abase him, and who it is that lieth. And watch! Lo! I am a watcher with you

11:94.ar: وَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمۡرُنَا نَجَّيۡنَا شُعَيۡبࣰ ا وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ بِرَحۡمَةࣲ مِّنَّا وَأَخَذَتِ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ ٱلصَّيۡحَةُ فَأَصۡبَحُواْ فِي دِيَٰرِهِمۡ جَٰثِمِينَ
11:94.en: And when Our commandment came to pass We saved Shu'eyb and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us; and the (Awful) Cry seized those who did injustice, and morning found them prostrate in their dwellings

11:95.ar: كَأَن لَّمۡ يَغۡنَوۡاْ فِيهَآۗ أَلَا بُعۡدࣰ ا لِّمَدۡيَنَ كَمَا بَعِدَتۡ ثَمُودُ
11:95.en: As though they had not dwelt there. A far removal for Midian, even as Thamud had been removed afar

11:96.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مُوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَسُلۡطَٰنࣲ مُّبِينٍ
11:96.en: And verily We sent Moses with Our revelations and a clear warrant

11:97.ar: إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِۦ فَٱتَّبَعُوٓاْ أَمۡرَ فِرۡعَوۡنَۖ وَمَآ أَمۡرُ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِرَشِيدࣲ‏
11:97.en: Unto Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they did follow the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was no right guide

11:98.ar: يَقۡدُمُ قَوۡمَهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ فَأَوۡرَدَهُمُ ٱلنَّارَۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡوِرۡدُ ٱلۡمَوۡرُودُ
11:98.en: He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them to the Fire for watering-place. Ah, hapless is the watering-place (whither they are) led

11:99.ar: وَأُتۡبِعُواْ فِي هَٰذِهِۦ لَعۡنَةࣰ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ بِئۡسَ ٱلرِّفۡدُ ٱلۡمَرۡفُودُ
11:99.en: A curse is made to follow them in the world and on the Day of Resurrection. Hapless is the gift (that will be) given (them)

11:100.ar: ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ نَقُصُّهُۥ عَلَيۡكَۖ مِنۡهَا قَآئِمࣱ وَحَصِيدࣱ‏
11:100.en: That is (something) of the tidings of the townships (which were destroyed of old). We relate it unto thee (Muhammad). Some of them are standing and some (already) reaped

11:101.ar: وَمَا ظَلَمۡنَٰهُمۡ وَلَٰكِن ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡۖ فَمَآ أَغۡنَتۡ عَنۡهُمۡ ءَالِهَتُهُمُ ٱلَّتِي يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲ لَّمَّا جَآءَ أَمۡرُ رَبِّكَۖ وَمَا زَادُوهُمۡ غَيۡرَ تَتۡبِيبࣲ‏
11:101.en: We wronged them not, but they did wrong themselves; and their gods on whom they call beside Allah availed them naught when came thy Lord's command; they added to them naught save ruin

11:102.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَخۡذُ رَبِّكَ إِذَآ أَخَذَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ وَهِيَ ظَٰلِمَةٌۚ إِنَّ أَخۡذَهُۥٓ أَلِيمࣱ شَدِيدٌ
11:102.en: Even thus is the grasp of thy Lord when He graspeth the townships while they are doing wrong. Lo! His grasp is painful, very strong

11:103.ar: إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّمَنۡ خَافَ عَذَابَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۚ ذَٰلِكَ يَوۡمࣱ مَّجۡمُوعࣱ لَّهُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَذَٰلِكَ يَوۡمࣱ مَّشۡهُودࣱ‏
11:103.en: Lo! herein verily there is a portent for those who fear the doom of the Hereafter. That is a day unto which mankind will be gathered, and that is a day that will be witnessed

11:104.en: And We defer it only to a term already reckoned

11:105.ar: يَوۡمَ يَأۡتِ لَا تَكَلَّمُ نَفۡسٌ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ فَمِنۡهُمۡ شَقِيࣱّ وَسَعِيدࣱ‏
11:105.en: On the day when it cometh no soul will speak except by His permission; some among them will be wretched, (others) glad

11:106.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ شَقُواْ فَفِي ٱلنَّارِ لَهُمۡ فِيهَا زَفِيرࣱ وَشَهِيقٌ
11:106.en: As for those who will be wretched (on that day) they will be in the Fire; sighing and wailing will be their portion therein

11:107.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ فَعَّالࣱ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ
11:107.en: Abiding there so long as the heavens and the earth endure save for that which thy Lord willeth. Lo! thy Lord is Doer of what He will

11:108.ar: ۞وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ سُعِدُواْ فَفِي ٱلۡجَنَّةِ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَۖ عَطَآءً غَيۡرَ مَجۡذُوذࣲ‏
11:108.en: And as for those who will be glad (that day) they will be in the Garden, abiding there so long as the heavens and the earth endure save for that which thy Lord willeth: a gift unfailing

11:112.ar: فَٱسۡتَقِمۡ كَمَآ أُمِرۡتَ وَمَن تَابَ مَعَكَ وَلَا تَطۡغَوۡاْۚ إِنَّهُۥ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
11:112.en: So tread thou the straight path as thou art commanded, and those who turn (unto Allah) with thee, and transgress not. Lo! He is Seer of what ye do

11:113.ar: وَلَا تَرۡكَنُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ فَتَمَسَّكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِنۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ثُمَّ لَا تُنصَرُونَ
11:113.en: And incline not toward those who do wrong lest the Fire touch you, and ye have no protecting friends against Allah, and afterward ye would not be helped

11:114.ar: وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ طَرَفَيِ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَزُلَفࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِۚ إِنَّ ٱلۡحَسَنَٰتِ يُذۡهِبۡنَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِۚ ذَٰلِكَ ذِكۡرَىٰ لِلذَّٰكِرِينَ
11:114.en: Establish worship at the two ends of the day and in some watches of the night. Lo! good deeds annul ill-deeds. This is reminder for the mindful

11:115.ar: وَٱصۡبِرۡ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجۡرَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
11:115.en: And have patience, (O Muhammad), for lo! Allah loseth not the wages of the good

11:116.ar: فَلَوۡلَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ أُوْلُواْ بَقِيَّةࣲ يَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡفَسَادِ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّمَّنۡ أَنجَيۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡۗ وَٱتَّبَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مَآ أُتۡرِفُواْ فِيهِ وَكَانُواْ مُجۡرِمِينَ
11:116.en: If only there had been among the generations before you men possessing a remnant (of good sense) to warn (their people) from corruption in the earth, as did a few of those whom We saved from them! The wrong-doers followed that by which they were made sapless, and were guilty

11:117.ar: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ بِظُلۡمࣲ وَأَهۡلُهَا مُصۡلِحُونَ
11:117.en: In truth thy Lord destroyed not the townships tyrannously while their folk were doing right

11:118.ar: وَلَوۡ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰۖ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ مُخۡتَلِفِينَ
11:118.en: And if thy Lord had willed, He verily would have made mankind one nation, yet they cease not differing

11:119.ar: إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ رَبُّكَۚ وَلِذَٰلِكَ خَلَقَهُمۡۗ وَتَمَّتۡ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ
11:119.en: Save him on whom thy Lord hath mercy; and for that He did create them. And the Word of thy Lord hath been fulfilled: Verily I shall fill hell with the jinn and mankind together

11:120.ar: وَكُلࣰّ ا نَّقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلرُّسُلِ مَا نُثَبِّتُ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَۚ وَجَآءَكَ فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَمَوۡعِظَةࣱ وَذِكۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
11:120.en: And all that We relate unto thee of the story of the messengers is in order that thereby We may make firm thy heart. And herein hath come unto thee the Truth and an exhortation and a reminder for believers

11:121.ar: وَقُل لِّلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱعۡمَلُواْ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُمۡ إِنَّا عَٰمِلُونَ
11:121.en: And say unto those who believe not: Act according to your power. Lo! We (too) are acting

11:122.en: And wait! Lo! We (too) are waiting

11:123.ar: وَلِلَّهِ غَيۡبُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِلَيۡهِ يُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ كُلُّهُۥ فَٱعۡبُدۡهُ وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَيۡهِۚ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
11:123.en: And Allah's is the Invisible of the heavens and the earth, and unto Him the whole matter will be returned. So worship Him and put thy trust in Him. Lo! thy Lord is not unaware of what ye (mortals) do

y-O8JgmzfKw.speaker: adnan
y-O8JgmzfKw.title: A Juz A Day, Juz 12: The End Is for the Believers
y-O8JgmzfKw.one_line: Surah Hud: the stories of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut and Shuayb reassure the Prophet that patient, steadfast believers win in the end.
y-O8JgmzfKw.summary: He opens with the Prophet's remark that Hud and its sister surahs turned his hair grey out of worry for his own people, then reads the surah's first verses as a summary of the Quran's message: worship Allah alone, seek forgiveness and resolve not to return, and a good life follows. Life is a test of the best deeds, where quality and sincerity outweigh quantity. He dwells on human fickleness, despairing when a blessing is removed and boasting when relief comes, against believers defined by patient endurance and steady good deeds. He then walks through the prophets in detail: Nuh's refusal to dismiss poor followers, the ark, and the son who was not of his family in faith; Hud and Salih facing people who cared more about ancestral custom than truth; Ibrahim's hospitality and tender pleading for Lut's people; Lut defending his guests; and Shuayb confronting fraud, whose words on seeking only reform he calls a motto for life. The lesson for the Prophet is patience, because the outcome belongs to the righteous. The closing commands are steadfastness, not leaning on wrongdoers, prayer whose good deeds erase and replace evil, and patience.

outline.heading: Opening
Hud and its sisters turned the Prophet grey
outline.gist: Stories of punished nations worried him for his own people, even those persecuting him.

outline.heading: Perfected verses: worship none but Allah
outline.gist: The disjointed letters lead into the Quran's miraculous nature; its core message is unfolded surah by surah.

outline.heading: Seek forgiveness, turn back, and live a good life
outline.gist: Asking forgiveness and resolving not to return brings wholesome enjoyment and due grace in this life and salvation in the next.

outline.heading: The Quran's message in four verses
outline.gist: Its majesty, exclusive worship, self-awareness of one's faults and repeated repentance unlock all good.

outline.heading: Every creature's provision and resting place
outline.gist: He knows what people hide and provides for every creature, knowing where it lives and dies.

outline.heading: His throne upon the water; creation in six days
outline.gist: The cosmos has order and purpose, and that purpose is to test us.

outline.heading: Best in deeds: quality over quantity
outline.gist: Quantity depends on time and circumstance; quality depends on sincerity and engagement, and that is the standard.

outline.heading: What is holding the punishment back?
outline.gist: Delay does not mean escape; when it comes nothing will avert it.

outline.heading: Despair when a blessing is taken away
outline.gist: Back at zero, not below it, the fickle person still sinks into gloom and forgets every other blessing.

outline.heading: Boasting when relief comes
outline.gist: After hardship lifts, they forget it and become proud as if untouchable.

outline.heading: Believers defined by patient endurance
outline.gist: In place of those who believe, the verse says those who are patient: rational and resilient, keeping their emotions in check and doing good.

outline.heading: Do not give up on the message
outline.gist: Their demands for treasure or an angel are not sincere; the Prophet is only a warner and Allah is the guardian of all affairs.

outline.heading: The challenge: produce ten surahs
outline.gist: The aim is not to win an argument but to lead to submission.

outline.heading: Those who want only this world
outline.gist: They are paid in full here, but good deeds done without worship carry no weight for salvation.

outline.heading: Humility as the believer's mark
outline.gist: True faith brings humility, in contrast to the materialist who cares only for this life.

outline.heading: The blind and deaf versus the seeing and hearing
outline.gist: A rhetorical question whose answer the audience supplies: they are not equal.

outline.heading: The six core prophets
outline.gist: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, Shuayb and Musa form the recurring group, with Nuh's story told here in most detail.

outline.heading: Nuh's call and the chiefs' contempt
outline.gist: They dismiss him as merely human and his followers as the lowliest fools.

outline.heading: No compulsion, no payment, no dismissing believers
outline.gist: He offers the message for them to consider, asks no money, and will not drive away believers because the elite dislike them.

outline.heading: I claim no treasures and no unseen
outline.gist: Calling a good person bad because he is poor would make Nuh the wrongdoer.

outline.heading: Bring on the punishment, then
outline.gist: Out of arguments, they demand the threat; Nuh says only Allah brings it.

outline.heading: An aside to Quraysh: did he fabricate it?
outline.gist: The narrative cuts to those listening in Makkah, who wonder how he knows these stories.

outline.heading: Building the ark amid mockery
outline.gist: Told none others will believe, Nuh builds a ship in dry land; if you laugh at us, we will laugh at you.

outline.heading: The oven bursts; board in the name of Allah
outline.gist: Pairs of every species and the believers board; the boarding dua is one to say on any vessel.

outline.heading: Nuh's son refuses and drowns
outline.gist: He seeks refuge on a mountain; the waters recede and the ark rests on Judi.

outline.heading: He is not of your family
outline.gist: Blood ties remain, but in this sense family means those who accepted the message; his whole life's conduct was unrighteous.

outline.heading: Nuh seeks forgiveness for asking
outline.gist: Even a gentle question felt like overstepping, so he asks for mercy.

outline.heading: A story of the unseen: be patient, the end is for the righteous
outline.gist: The purpose of the story is to reassure the Prophet that the believers will win.

outline.heading: Neither he nor his people knew it before
outline.gist: No one in Makkah knew these stories, so they could not be copied; later corroboration made them more striking.

outline.heading: Hud: repentance brings rain and added strength
outline.gist: He gives Ad reasons to worship Allah and asks no reward.

outline.heading: Plot against me; I trust in Allah
outline.gist: Accused of being possessed by their gods, he disowns their idols, trusts Allah and says Allah will replace them.

outline.heading: Rejecting one messenger is rejecting all
outline.gist: Ad met only Hud, yet are said to have disobeyed the messengers; they followed every stubborn tyrant.

outline.heading: Salih: we had high hopes for you
outline.gist: Thamud's objection was not about Allah's worth but about leaving the traditions of their forefathers.

outline.heading: The she-camel and the blast
outline.gist: They killed the demanded sign, were given three days, and vanished as if they had never lived there.

outline.heading: The angels greet Ibrahim with salam
outline.gist: Saying salam alone is a complete greeting.

outline.heading: A roasted calf and an untouched meal
outline.gist: A generous host, Ibrahim grew fearful because assassins would not eat their target's food.

outline.heading: Glad tidings of Ishaq and Yaqub
outline.gist: His barren, elderly wife is astonished; nothing is beyond Allah's decree.

outline.heading: Ibrahim pleads for Lut's people
outline.gist: Ignoring his own good news, the tender-hearted Ibrahim argues for others until told the decree cannot be averted.

outline.heading: Lut's distress for his guests
outline.gist: He fears his predatory people will assault the handsome visitors and points them to the women of the town as a purer path.

outline.heading: Leave by night; the cities overturned
outline.gist: The angels reveal themselves; Lut leaves with his believing family except his wife, and stones of baked clay fall at dawn.

outline.heading: Shuayb confronts cheating and fraud
outline.gist: After tawhid he addresses the society's real ill: give full measure, do not defraud, and honest gain is better.

outline.heading: Does your prayer tell us how to run our wealth?
outline.gist: They mock his prayer for meddling in their business.

outline.heading: I only want reform as far as I can
outline.gist: He will not do what he forbids, seeks only to make things better, and credits all success to Allah: a motto for life.

outline.heading: More regard for my clan than for Allah
outline.gist: He appeals to logic, emotion and precedent; they threaten to stone him, and the blast takes Madyan.

outline.heading: Musa and Pharaoh leading his people into the fire
outline.gist: They followed his misguided command, and he will lead them on the Day.

outline.heading: We did not wrong them; fear the torment of the Hereafter
outline.gist: Such is His grip on societies entrenched in wrong; today's trials are tests, and the greater fear is the Hereafter.

outline.heading: The miserable and the joyful
outline.gist: Sighing and gasping in the fire versus an unending gift in paradise.

outline.heading: Be steadfast as you are commanded
outline.gist: Like the prophets before him, the Prophet and those with him must stay the course without transgressing.

outline.heading: Do not lean on the wrongdoers
outline.gist: Relying on them invites the fire, as Nuh's son showed.

outline.heading: Establish the prayer at both ends of the day
outline.gist: A reference to the five daily prayers, a pillar whose good deeds erase evil ones.

outline.heading: Good deeds remove the very desire for evil
outline.gist: The good gradually takes the place of evil in a person's life until little or none remains.

outline.heading: Be patient; Allah never destroys a righteous town
outline.gist: The reward of the good is never lost, and the destroyed nations were committed to evil.

outline.heading: Created to choose freely
outline.gist: Allah could have made one community; He gave agency, and choices carry consequences.

outline.heading: Stories to steady the heart; worship and trust Him
outline.gist: A warning for disbelievers and a reminder for believers; persist, wait and rely on Allah.

outline.heading: Surah Yusuf's mirrored structure
outline.gist: Events unfold and then unroll in reverse, oscillating between hardship and ease until the believer comes out on top.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Prophets
themes.note: Six prophets carry the same call against contempt, tradition, fraud and immorality, and are saved while their opponents perish.

themes.label: Patience and resilience
themes.note: Fickle people swing between despair and pride; believers are defined by patient endurance and steady good deeds.

themes.label: Steadfastness
themes.note: Be steadfast, do not lean on wrongdoers, keep the prayer and be patient.

themes.label: Tawbah
themes.note: Seeking forgiveness and resolving not to return is the path to a good life.

themes.label: Sincerity and quality of deeds
themes.note: Allah tests who is best in deeds, measured by sincerity rather than amount.

themes.label: Sincerity
themes.note: Good done only for worldly gain carries no weight in the Hereafter.

themes.label: Family and faith
themes.note: Nuh's son was not of his family in the sense of faith, though blood ties remain.

themes.label: Reform
themes.note: Shuayb tackles his society's specific corruption and seeks only reform as far as he is able.

themes.label: Prayer
themes.note: Prayer's good deeds erase sins and replace the desire for evil.

hadith.gist: When a companion noticed his grey hairs, the Prophet said Hud and its sister surahs had made him grey

maxims: Quality matters more than quantity
Patient endurance is the marker of true iman
I only want reform as far as I can
Rejecting one messenger is rejecting all of them
In the end, the believers win

stories.who: Nuh, the ark and his son
stories.point: Patience through long rejection is rewarded; faith, not blood alone, decides who is saved.

stories.who: Hud and Ad
stories.point: Repentance brings strength; he trusts Allah against his people's plots.

stories.who: Salih and Thamud
stories.point: Attachment to ancestral custom blinded them; they killed the sign they demanded.

stories.who: Ibrahim and the angels
stories.point: Generous hospitality and a tender heart that pleads even for a doomed people.

stories.who: Lut and his guests
stories.point: He stands alone to protect his guests and is saved with his believing family.

stories.who: Shuayb and Madyan
stories.point: A prophet who names his society's fraud and seeks only reform.

takeaways: Seek forgiveness and resolve not to return to the sin
Focus on the sincerity and quality of your deeds
Stay patient and rational through loss and through relief
Never look down on people for being poor
Keep the prayer so good deeds gradually replace bad ones

2:183.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:183.en: O ye who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil)

59alS6BlE-0.speaker: adnan
59alS6BlE-0.speaker_note: MWN Friday khutbah on 9 Ramadan in his usual mixed Arabic-English delivery; recalls his own weeks of mulazamah with Sheikh Shukri at sixteen; no other speaker named
59alS6BlE-0.title: Second Week of Ramadan: Establishing the New Standard
59alS6BlE-0.one_line: Use the second week of Ramadan to build new lifelong standards by modelling your ordinary day on the Prophet's ordinary day, imitating him partially where you cannot fully.
59alS6BlE-0.summary: Starting from 2:183, fasting was prescribed so that you may attain taqwa, he notes how the Quran attaches purposes to its commands and makes Ramadan's purpose the forced change of habits. After one week the anxiety of working while fasting is gone, and this is exactly when people start dropping off taraweeh; instead it is the time to build a new standard. His method is to take a snapshot of the Prophet's ordinary day, not a battle or an Eid. He recalls mulazamah, the practice of living with a scholar for weeks, which he did at sixteen with Sheikh Shukri, who barely ate or slept and filled every half hour of transit with dhikr; anyone can act well for a day, but the mask drops after weeks, and the Sahabah lived with the Prophet for years. He then walks through the Prophet's day from several narrations: Isha, a late conversation with Abu Bakr or family, early sleep in the pattern of Dawud, never a whole night awake, Fajr in congregation, the markets after Fajr, walking with widows and the poor, a midday rest, chores at home, and dhikr, dua, visits and smiles as the fillers that made ordinary days extraordinary. He warns against 3 a.m. qiyam followed by seven coffees. In the second khutbah he quotes Aisha that none can match the Prophet's capacity, so imitate partially: ten minutes before Fajr, three fasts a month, a moist tongue. Unlike ascetics who lost moderation, his life was normal yet full of Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
Fasting prescribed so that you may attain taqwa
outline.gist: 2:183, then the Quran's recurring 'so that you may' clauses (attain taqwa, be guided, remember, reason, succeed, be rightly guided, reflect) show that its commands come with stated purposes.

outline.heading: Week two: the fear is gone, time to build
outline.gist: After a week of fasting at work there is no more anxiety and Allah has granted a new peace, yet this is when people start dropping off taraweeh. No excuses: this is the time to build new standards and a new way of life.

outline.heading: A snapshot of the Prophet's ordinary day
outline.gist: Not a battle day or an Eid, but how he spent his normal 24 hours across his life. None of us can live exactly as he did, but Ramadan offers a unique chance to adjust towards it.

outline.heading: Mulazamah with Sheikh Shukri
outline.gist: Living with a scholar for weeks: at sixteen he waited for Sheikh Shukri to visit his daughter so he could eat a whole chicken and sleep, because the sheikh barely ate or slept and filled every idle half hour in transit with dhikr or Quran. Anyone can act well for a day; over weeks the mask drops.

outline.heading: Ramadan is not at your whim
outline.gist: The Sahabah had years of companionship with the Prophet. Ramadan imposes changes whether you like it or not, to drop bad habits and pick up new ones: zoom out on your life, pick what to improve, and come one step closer to his lifestyle every year.

outline.heading: After Isha: staying up with Abu Bakr
outline.gist: Umar's report that the Prophet would pray Isha and then stay up with Abu Bakr over some matter of the Muslims; he was sent to all of humanity and carried its affairs.

outline.heading: Evening talk with family
outline.gist: Aisha: he would go to one of his wives' houses where people gathered and he would talk with them, then retire to his bed.

outline.heading: Early sleep and the prayer of Dawud
outline.gist: He slept in the first part of the night and followed Dawud's pattern: sleep half the night, pray a third, sleep a sixth, so in a hypothetical ten-hour night most is sleep, then prayer, then a little more sleep before Fajr.

outline.heading: Never a whole night: the 3 a.m. trap
outline.gist: Night prayer always came after sleep; Aisha: he never stood a whole night in prayer. Staying up until 3 a.m. in Ramadan and then chugging seven coffees to get through school is not his way and will catch up with you.

outline.heading: Sleep after taraweeh, rise before Fajr
outline.gist: Bad sleep hygiene takes away years, mental health and physical health, even from those in their twenties who feel invincible. Go home and sleep after taraweeh, wake a little before Fajr for a few rak'ahs, and pray Fajr in congregation.

outline.heading: After Fajr: the markets
outline.gist: Al-Nasa'i's narration: he went to the markets of the Muslims, commanding, forbidding, advising, settling matters between them, teaching halal and haram and meeting their needs.

outline.heading: Much dhikr, short khutbahs, walking with the widow
outline.gist: Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa: he made much dhikr and little idle talk, lengthened the prayer and shortened the khutbah, and never disdained walking with a widow or a poor person to settle their need.

outline.heading: Midday rest and work at home
outline.gist: A midday rest, hard to fit into today's workforce, then home: Aisha describes him visiting the sick, milking his goat, mending his sandal, serving his family and patching his garment until Maghrib.

outline.heading: What made his ordinary days different: the fillers
outline.gist: Most days, his included, are ordinary; he had extraordinary days running a new state everyone wanted to destroy, but what set his days apart were the fillers: subhanallah, alhamdulillah, la ilaha illallah, Allahu akbar, hasbiyallah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah, dua, and time given to people.

outline.heading: A face that was always smiling
outline.gist: He was bright-faced, smiling and joking with people despite the burdens he carried from every side, so the companions knew something was wrong on the rare days his face changed.

outline.heading: Your day: a new standard that outlasts Eid
outline.gist: Look at your day and ask what you can improve and what Ramadan has already improved. Do not flip back to how things were on the day of Eid. Mindfulness means not being distracted from Allah; it feels hard at first for a heart not yet mindful of Him.

outline.heading: Second khutbah: imitate him partially
outline.gist: Aisha: none of you can bear what the Prophet bore. Full imitation is too hard for his followers, but partial imitation is possible: what cannot be attained wholly should not be abandoned wholly.

outline.heading: Ramadan compels change
outline.gist: One purpose of the month is that Allah forces us to change our habits: suhoor breaks your sleep, a day without food changes metabolism, slows you down and reins in desire, and nearly everyone prays some taraweeh. Let it build a system of life resembling his.

outline.heading: Substitutes within reach
outline.gist: Ten minutes before Fajr instead of a third of the night; three fasts a month or Mondays and Thursdays instead of alternate days; a tongue kept moist with dhikr and Quran; spare time filled with visiting the sick, kinship, advice and meeting someone's need.

outline.heading: Ascetics who lost moderation
outline.gist: Buddhist monks and Hindu ascetics live lives no sane person could, without food, drink, marriage or speech, because they lost the middle way. He fasted and ate, slept, married, joked and laughed with his family, yet his life was full of love of Allah.

outline.heading: Small changes, not back-breaking ones
outline.gist: He is not asking for changes that break your back or ruin your family life, only the small ones Ramadan offers, to build and establish the new standard.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: Ramadan is the yearly chance to establish new lifelong standards: zoom out on your day, pick what to improve, and let the forced changes of the month become habits that bring you a step closer to the Prophet's lifestyle each year.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: A snapshot of the Prophet's ordinary day from Isha to Maghrib, built from narrations: early sleep, night prayer in Dawud's pattern, Fajr, the markets, service to widows and the poor, home chores, constant dhikr and a smiling face, all within a balanced, normal life.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: By week two fasting at work holds no fear, so this is the moment not to drop off but to build; Ramadan was legislated with a purpose, taqwa, and it forces habit change whether you like it or not.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Suhoor breaks your sleep, fasting changes metabolism and calms desires, and everyone prays at least some taraweeh; one of the purposes of the month is to compel change.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: The Prophet's Isha, early sleep, qiyam after rest in the pattern of Dawud, never a whole night, and Fajr in congregation; he recommends sleeping after taraweeh and rising shortly before Fajr for a few rak'ahs.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: The fillers made the Prophet's ordinary days different: dhikr formulas, dua and care for people in every gap; mindfulness is not being distracted from Allah, and a heart not yet mindful finds it hard at first.

themes.label: Moderation and balance (wasatiyyah)
themes.note: Imitate partially where you cannot fully. Buddhist and Hindu ascetics lost moderation and live impossible lives; the Prophet fasted and ate, slept, married, joked and laughed, yet filled his life with love of Allah.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Mulazamah, living with a scholar for weeks, hardly possible in the West; his teenage weeks with Sheikh Shukri showed a life packed with teaching and service where every idle half hour was filled.

themes.label: Mental health, anxiety and emotional wellbeing
themes.note: Staying up until 3 a.m. and surviving on seven coffees is bad sleep hygiene that steals years, mental health and physical health, even from those in their twenties who feel invincible.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)
themes.note: Despite carrying a new state everyone wanted to destroy, he was always bright-faced, smiling and joking, so that a changed expression told the companions something was wrong.

themes.label: Visiting the sick, caring for elders and the vulnerable
themes.note: He walked with widows and the poor to settle their needs and visited the sick as part of his routine; he asks listeners to fill their time the same way.

themes.label: Taqwa and God-consciousness
themes.note: Fasting was prescribed so that you may attain taqwa; the Quran's purpose clauses show what each command is meant to produce.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: Do not sit idle: keep the tongue moist with dhikr and Quran and fill empty time with a sick person to visit, a relative to reach, advice to give or a need to meet.

quran.point: Fasting is prescribed on you as on those before you so that you may attain taqwa; the opening verse and the model of the Quran's purpose clauses.

hadith.gist: Umar: the Prophet would pray Isha and then stay up with Abu Bakr over some matter of the Muslims, and Umar was with them.
Aisha: he would go to one of his wives' houses where people gathered and he would talk with them, then retire to his bed in the first part of the night.
The prayer of Dawud, which he calls sahih: sleep half the night, pray a third and sleep a sixth; and Aisha's report that the Prophet never stood a whole night in prayer.
After Fajr the Prophet would go to the markets of the Muslims, commanding, forbidding, advising and settling their needs.
Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa: he made much dhikr and little idle talk, lengthened the prayer and shortened the khutbah, and did not disdain walking with a widow or a poor person to settle their need.
Aisha: he would visit the sick, milk his goat, mend his sandal, serve his family and patch his garment.
Aisha: none of you is capable of what the Messenger of Allah was capable of; hence partial imitation.

maxims: Ramadan is not at your whim
Easy to act for a day; the mask drops after weeks
What makes the day different is the fillers
What cannot be attained wholly should not be abandoned wholly
Every Ramadan, one step closer to his life
Don't flip back on the day of Eid

stories.who: His mulazamah with Sheikh Shukri at sixteen
stories.point: Living with a scholar for weeks exposed a life with almost no food or sleep and every spare half hour filled with dhikr; a mask cannot last that long, which is why companionship over time reveals and transmits character.

stories.who: The Prophet's ordinary day
stories.point: Reconstructed from several narrations, his routine was mostly ordinary; what distinguished it were the fillers of dhikr, service and a smiling face.

stories.who: Students up until 3 a.m. on seven coffees
stories.point: Late qiyam that ruins the next day is not the prophetic pattern; sleep first, then rise shortly before Fajr.

stories.who: Buddhist monks and Hindu ascetics
stories.point: Lives without food, drink, marriage or speech show what happens when moderation is lost; the Prophet lived a normal life that was nonetheless full of Allah.

contemporary: 9 Ramadan 1447; attendance at taraweeh typically dropping off in the second week
Mulazamah with scholars, common in the Middle East, hardly possible in the West; his weeks with Sheikh Shukri
Students praying qiyam at 3 a.m. and getting through school on seven coffees; sleep hygiene and mental health
takeaways: Do not drop off taraweeh in the second week; stop making excuses and use the month to build a new standard for your life.
Sleep after Isha and taraweeh instead of staying up until 3 a.m., wake a little before Fajr for a few rak'ahs and pray Fajr in congregation.
Fill empty minutes with dhikr and Quran, and spare time with service: visiting the sick, keeping kinship ties, giving advice, helping someone in need.
Where you cannot imitate the Prophet fully, imitate him partially: fast three days a month or Mondays and Thursdays, pray ten minutes before Fajr.
Keep a balanced, normal life of eating, sleeping, family and laughter, but fill its gaps with Allah, and keep the changes after Eid.

36:33.ar: وَءَايَةࣱ لَّهُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةُ أَحۡيَيۡنَٰهَا وَأَخۡرَجۡنَا مِنۡهَا حَبࣰّ ا فَمِنۡهُ يَأۡكُلُونَ
36:33.en: A token unto them is the dead earth. We revive it, and We bring forth from it grain so that they eat thereof

36:34.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا فِيهَا جَنَّٰتࣲ مِّن نَّخِيلࣲ وَأَعۡنَٰبࣲ وَفَجَّرۡنَا فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلۡعُيُونِ
36:34.en: And We have placed therein gardens of the date-palm and grapes, and We have caused springs of water to gush forth therein

36:35.ar: لِيَأۡكُلُواْ مِن ثَمَرِهِۦ وَمَا عَمِلَتۡهُ أَيۡدِيهِمۡۚ أَفَلَا يَشۡكُرُونَ
36:35.en: That they may eat of the fruit thereof, and their hands made it not. Will they not, then, give thanks

36:36.ar: سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡأَزۡوَٰجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمِنۡ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
36:36.en: Glory be to Him Who created all the sexual pairs, of that which the earth groweth, and of themselves, and of that which they know not

36:37.ar: وَءَايَةࣱ لَّهُمُ ٱلَّيۡلُ نَسۡلَخُ مِنۡهُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فَإِذَا هُم مُّظۡلِمُونَ
36:37.en: A token unto them is night. We strip it of the day, and lo! they are in darkness

36:38.ar: وَٱلشَّمۡسُ تَجۡرِي لِمُسۡتَقَرࣲّ لَّهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقۡدِيرُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡعَلِيمِ
36:38.en: And the sun runneth on unto a resting-place for him. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Wise

36:39.ar: وَٱلۡقَمَرَ قَدَّرۡنَٰهُ مَنَازِلَ حَتَّىٰ عَادَ كَٱلۡعُرۡجُونِ ٱلۡقَدِيمِ
36:39.en: And for the moon We have appointed mansions till she return like an old shrivelled palm-leaf

36:40.ar: لَا ٱلشَّمۡسُ يَنۢبَغِي لَهَآ أَن تُدۡرِكَ ٱلۡقَمَرَ وَلَا ٱلَّيۡلُ سَابِقُ ٱلنَّهَارِۚ وَكُلࣱّ فِي فَلَكࣲ يَسۡبَحُونَ
36:40.en: It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor doth the night outstrip the day. They float each in an orbit

36:41.ar: وَءَايَةࣱ لَّهُمۡ أَنَّا حَمَلۡنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡفُلۡكِ ٱلۡمَشۡحُونِ
36:41.en: And a token unto them is that We bear their offspring in the laden ship

36:42.ar: وَخَلَقۡنَا لَهُم مِّن مِّثۡلِهِۦ مَا يَرۡكَبُونَ
36:42.en: And have created for them of the like thereof whereon they ride

36:43.ar: وَإِن نَّشَأۡ نُغۡرِقۡهُمۡ فَلَا صَرِيخَ لَهُمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنقَذُونَ
36:43.en: And if We will, We drown them, and there is no help for them, neither can they be saved

36:44.ar: إِلَّا رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنَّا وَمَتَٰعًا إِلَىٰ حِينࣲ‏
36:44.en: Unless by mercy from Us and as comfort for a while

uSdlFO4fnQw.speaker: adnan
uSdlFO4fnQw.speaker_note: continues his own Yasin series; mentions his father leaving Syria and his own children
uSdlFO4fnQw.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 4 (33-44)
uSdlFO4fnQw.one_line: Three signs that bring a heart to life: the revived earth, the precise heavens, and the ark, with what saying Subhan Allah truly means.
uSdlFO4fnQw.summary: After the believer's story, he says the surah now teaches how to gain a living heart, starting with noticing Allah's signs. The signs are simple and need no degree, only attention we have dulled, just as we take family for granted and resent our children for taking their privileges for granted.
