He urges using fasting days to sit outside and contemplate, lamenting a generation that has lost daydreaming to screens. The first passage is the dead earth given life: you plant and water, but you cannot make the seed grow, so be grateful, and know Allah can revive a dead heart the same way. He then explains Subhan Allah as the Muslim's core stance: Allah is not questioned; you question yourself and change what you can, and this protects the soul in times of grief. The second passage looks upward: night drawn out of day, the sun's course, the moon's phases like a dried palm stalk, all in precise orbits without which no life would exist, and none of it under our control. The third passage turns to history: the ark of Nuh and the ships that let humanity travel and share knowledge, things that need not have worked. He lists life, the universe, history and personal experience as sources of iman pointing to one Creator, and asks people to stop and appreciate before rushing on.

outline.heading: The believer lived by different values
outline.gist: His choice was hard to justify rationally because he lived by values most people have not embraced; no one had to assign him responsibility.

outline.heading: What the Prophet brought: spiritual life
outline.gist: The companions were physically alive but had never tasted spiritual life; once they did, it was hard to go back.

outline.heading: Heraclius and Abu Sufyan: faith that mixes with the heart
outline.gist: Heraclius learned that no follower left the Prophet's religion, because faith once mixed with the heart is never given up.

outline.heading: A living heart starts by recognizing signs
outline.gist: The signs need no degree, only the attentiveness most of us outgrow or become numb to.

outline.heading: Taking family and privilege for granted
outline.gist: We take spouses, children and parents for granted, and dislike it when our children ignore privileges that are not the norm in the world.

outline.heading: Use the fasting day to contemplate
outline.gist: Not looking down at food leaves time to look up; sit outside and actually think about what you see every day.

outline.heading: The lost art of daydreaming
outline.gist: He misses staring at rain or clouds; this generation is deprived of simply observing because of screens.

outline.heading: The dead earth brought to life, like a dead heart
outline.gist: Just as Allah revives dead earth and brings grain from it, He can revive a heart, and others will benefit from it.

outline.heading: Gardens and springs not made by their hands
outline.gist: He weighs the reading that their hands made it and prefers that they did not make it, given the call to gratitude that follows.

outline.heading: What if the seed does not grow?
outline.gist: Farmers control everything except the one thing all else rests on, that the seed sprouts; whose laws are these?

outline.heading: He can bring your heart to life too
outline.gist: The verse began with Allah giving life so that you do not despair of your own heart.

outline.heading: Exalted is He who created all pairs
outline.gist: Subhan means Allah is flawless, the source of all good; He created pairs in plants, people and things we do not know.

outline.heading: Subhan Allah: question yourself, not Allah
outline.gist: The Muslim's distinctive view of the divine: Allah is beyond our standards; when something is wrong you question yourself and change what you can.

outline.heading: Tasbih protects you in times of sorrow
outline.gist: Repeating Subhan Allah trains the self not to turn on Allah when pain comes, accepting His decree in ease and difficulty.

outline.heading: We are being tested, not Allah
outline.gist: The Prophet lived magnifying Allah; life is a trial of our role, not of how well God manages the universe.

outline.heading: Nature documentaries as religious time
outline.gist: He has his children watch biology documentaries because observing creation fills you with awe at its depth and variety.

outline.heading: Night stripped from the day: darkness is the norm
outline.gist: Night is drawn out like an animal shedding its skin; outside the atmosphere darkness is the norm and daylight the exception.

outline.heading: The sun runs to its resting place; al-Aziz, the unfathomable
outline.gist: Whatever you can break down and fully understand is a creation, not God.

outline.heading: The moon's phases and the old palm stalk
outline.gist: Months come from the moon, which returns to a crescent like a dried, curved palm branch.

outline.heading: Sun and moon each swimming in its orbit
outline.gist: The sun will not overtake the moon nor night overpower day; each moves in its own course.

outline.heading: A delicate balance that makes life possible
outline.gist: Precise distances and orbits allow life; far from the equator life is harder and depression higher, as winters here show.

outline.heading: A source of energy you do not control
outline.gist: The sun blasts the earth with energy every day; if it failed to rise, all our quarrels would stop, yet we take it for granted.

outline.heading: Seeing a sign, not just the sun
outline.gist: The life of the heart is seeing the sun as a sign of Allah, all of it placed in your service.

outline.heading: The sources of iman all point to one Creator
outline.gist: Life, the universe, history and personal experience each point in the same direction, toward one Creator.

outline.heading: We carried their ancestors in the laden ark
outline.gist: Humanity survives through those carried with Nuh; the history of our existence is itself a sign.

outline.heading: Shared basics across world religions
outline.gist: Faiths with no contact share a creator, reward and punishment, a first couple and a first sin, because the history is the same.

outline.heading: Vessels like the ark to carry them
outline.gist: Allah made ships so people could cross continents, discover places and meet others.

outline.heading: If We willed, We would drown them: why does anything float?
outline.gist: Buoyancy is His law; had it not held, no travel or exchange of knowledge would exist. He lets us enjoy it out of mercy for a time.

outline.heading: Travel, look and appreciate first
outline.gist: See the world's diversity and pause to appreciate it before the restaurant; do not keep the trait you dislike in your children.

outline.heading: Precisely placed for you
outline.gist: He reviews the revived land, the right-sized sun and single moon, and the ships, none of which you planned.

outline.heading: How to gain the believer's life
outline.gist: After the man who was killed yet is alive, Allah shows the way to that life: start by appreciating His signs.

themes.label: Contemplating Allah's signs in creation (tafakkur)
themes.note: A living heart begins by noticing simple signs: the revived earth, the heavens' precision and the ships.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: We control none of what sustains us, from sprouting seeds to sunrise, so at least be grateful.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Taking spouses, parents and children for granted, and children taking privilege for granted.

themes.label: Technology, AI, social media and attention
themes.note: Screens have deprived a generation of daydreaming and observation.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Subhan as declaring Allah flawless and beyond our standards; al-Aziz as the unfathomable whose essence cannot be broken down.

themes.label: Contentment and acceptance (ridha)
themes.note: Do not question Allah in pain; question yourself, change what you can and accept His decree.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Life, the universe, history and experience as sources of iman all pointing to one Creator.

hadith.gist: Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan whether any of the Prophet's followers left his religion; told no, he said that is how faith is once its joy mixes with the heart.

maxims: You just have to be alive to see these signs
We're being tested, not Allah
Whatever you can break down is not God
You don't just see the sun, you see a sign

stories.who: Heraclius questioning Abu Sufyan
stories.point: Faith that has entered the heart is never given up.

stories.who: Nuh and the ark
stories.point: All humanity descends from those carried; history itself is a sign.

stories.who: His father choosing to emigrate from Syria to Canada
stories.point: A light-hearted note on how much climate and sunlight shape human life.

contemporary: BBC nature documentaries
Screens and tablets replacing daydreaming
High rates of depression in northern climates
AI as the latest product of centuries of exchanged knowledge
takeaways: Spend part of each fasting day sitting outside and contemplating creation.
Stop taking family and everyday blessings for granted.
When hardship hits, say Subhan Allah and question your own choices rather than Allah.
Watch nature with your children as a way to build awe of Allah.
When you travel, pause to appreciate what Allah made before rushing to enjoy it.

9:64.ar: يَحۡذَرُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ أَن تُنَزَّلَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ سُورَةࣱ تُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡۚ قُلِ ٱسۡتَهۡزِءُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡرِجࣱ مَّا تَحۡذَرُونَ
9:64.en: The hypocrites fear lest a surah should be revealed concerning them, proclaiming what is in their hearts. Say: Scoff (your fill)! Lo! Allah is disclosing what ye fear

9:65.ar: وَلَئِن سَأَلۡتَهُمۡ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّمَا كُنَّا نَخُوضُ وَنَلۡعَبُۚ قُلۡ أَبِٱللَّهِ وَءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَرَسُولِهِۦ كُنتُمۡ تَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
9:65.en: And if thou ask them (O Muhammad) they will say: We did but talk and jest. Say: Was it at Allah and His revelations and His messenger that ye did scoff

9:66.ar: لَا تَعۡتَذِرُواْ قَدۡ كَفَرۡتُم بَعۡدَ إِيمَٰنِكُمۡۚ إِن نَّعۡفُ عَن طَآئِفَةࣲ مِّنكُمۡ نُعَذِّبۡ طَآئِفَةَۢ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ مُجۡرِمِينَ
9:66.en: Make no excuse. Ye have disbelieved after your (confession of) belief. If We forgive a party of you, a party of you We shall punish because they have been guilty

9:101.ar: وَمِمَّنۡ حَوۡلَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابِ مُنَٰفِقُونَۖ وَمِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ مَرَدُواْ عَلَى ٱلنِّفَاقِ لَا تَعۡلَمُهُمۡۖ نَحۡنُ نَعۡلَمُهُمۡۚ سَنُعَذِّبُهُم مَّرَّتَيۡنِ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَذَابٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
9:101.en: And among those around you of the wandering Arabs there are hypocrites, and among the townspeople of Al-Madinah (there are some who) persist in hypocrisy whom thou (O Muhammad) knowest not. We, We know them, and We shall chastise them twice; then they will be relegated to a painful doom

9:102.ar: وَءَاخَرُونَ ٱعۡتَرَفُواْ بِذُنُوبِهِمۡ خَلَطُواْ عَمَلࣰ ا صَٰلِحࣰ ا وَءَاخَرَ سَيِّئًا عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
9:102.en: And (there are) others who have acknowledged their faults. They mixed a righteous action with another that was bad. It may be that Allah will relent toward them. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

9:103.ar: خُذۡ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ صَدَقَةࣰ تُطَهِّرُهُمۡ وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا وَصَلِّ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ إِنَّ صَلَوٰتَكَ سَكَنࣱ لَّهُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
9:103.en: Take alms of their wealth, wherewith thou mayst purify them and mayst make them grow, and pray for them. Lo! thy prayer is an assuagement for them. Allah is Hearer, Knower

9:104.ar: أَلَمۡ يَعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ يَقۡبَلُ ٱلتَّوۡبَةَ عَنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَأۡخُذُ ٱلصَّدَقَٰتِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
9:104.en: Know they not that Allah is He Who accepteth repentance from His bondmen and taketh the alms, and that Allah is He Who is the Relenting, the Merciful

9:105.ar: وَقُلِ ٱعۡمَلُواْ فَسَيَرَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمۡ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَۖ وَسَتُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَٰلِمِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
9:105.en: And say (unto them): Act! Allah will behold your actions, and (so will) His messenger and the believers, and ye will be brought back to the Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, and He will tell you what ye used to do

9:106.ar: وَءَاخَرُونَ مُرۡجَوۡنَ لِأَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ إِمَّا يُعَذِّبُهُمۡ وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيۡهِمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
9:106.en: And (there are) others who await Allah's decree, whether He will punish them or will forgive them. Allah is Knower, Wise

9:117.ar: لَّقَد تَّابَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ وَٱلۡأَنصَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ فِي سَاعَةِ ٱلۡعُسۡرَةِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا كَادَ يَزِيغُ قُلُوبُ فَرِيقࣲ مِّنۡهُمۡ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ بِهِمۡ رَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
9:117.en: Allah hath turned in mercy to the Prophet, and to the Muhajirin and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship. After the hearts of a party of them had almost swerved aside, then turned He unto them in mercy. Lo! He is Full of Pity, Merciful for them

9:118.ar: وَعَلَى ٱلثَّلَٰثَةِ ٱلَّذِينَ خُلِّفُواْ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتۡ وَضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَن لَّا مَلۡجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّآ إِلَيۡهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لِيَتُوبُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
9:118.en: And to the three also (did He turn in mercy) who were left behind, when the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for them, and their own souls were straitened for them till they bethought them that there is no refuge from Allah save toward Him. Then turned He unto them in mercy that they (too) might turn (repentant unto Him). Lo! Allah! He is the Relenting, the Merciful

9:119.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَكُونُواْ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
9:119.en: O ye who believe! Be careful of your duty to Allah, and be with the truthful

Gjj4y3FE1VQ.speaker: adnan
Gjj4y3FE1VQ.speaker_note: Sh. Adnan's Ramadan halqa series on his channel; same voice and format as the other nights
Gjj4y3FE1VQ.title: Tawbah (Ramadan 2026, Night 10: Quranic Themes 2)
Gjj4y3FE1VQ.one_line: What real repentance requires, read through three passages of Surat al-Tawbah: the mocking hypocrites, the three groups around Medina, and Ka'b ibn Malik.
Gjj4y3FE1VQ.summary: He opens by defining tawbah: not carried guilt but an honest admission that something was wrong, real remorse, and a plan, however imperfect, to remove at least one factor that makes the sin easy. Repentance without these is not serious, which is why people who never believed their habit was a problem relapse. He then reads rarely explained verses about hypocrites who mocked Allah, His signs and His Prophet and called it a joke. Allah refused their apology, even though the door of repentance stays open until death, because mocking the sacred needs full repentance, a turning of one's whole life. He tells young people to leave gatherings where the deen is mocked, and recounts the hadith of the man who found his lost camel to show Allah's joy at repentance. The verses about the people around Medina describe three groups: entrenched hypocrites who are dead weight in a community, those who admit their sins and mix good with bad, and the indifferent whose fate is deferred. He asks everyone to give more than they take and to be in the middle group. The story of Ka'b ibn Malik closes the night: he refused to lie, endured fifty days of boycott, burned a king's invitation, and found that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him.

outline.heading: Remorse, not guilt
outline.gist: Tawbah is an acknowledgement that what you did was wrong, producing useful remorse; people who relapse after rehab often never believed their habit was a problem.

outline.heading: Tawbah needs a plan
outline.gist: Without remorse and a plan you will go back; the plan need not be perfect but must remove at least one factor that makes the sin easy, such as time with a certain person. Wrongs against people need restitution, a separate topic.

outline.heading: Hypocrites fear being exposed
outline.gist: Heavy verses rarely explained: the hypocrites feared a surah revealing what was in their hearts, and Allah exposes them, often through their own behaviour, because the mask eventually falls.

outline.heading: 'We were only joking'
outline.gist: Asked about their mockery, they said they were just playing; he asks why, of everything one could laugh at, they chose Allah, His signs and His Prophet.

outline.heading: Leave gatherings that mock the deen
outline.gist: He tells young people to walk away from groups that belittle Allah, the Prophet or the deen, without picking fights, because the next verse treats such mockery as disbelief; the hypocrites only went along with religion for social reasons.

outline.heading: When an apology is not accepted
outline.gist: The door of tawbah is open until death and until the sun rises from the west, yet here Allah says 'make no excuse': mocking the divine needs repentance, not a quick apology.

outline.heading: Tawbah is turning your life around
outline.gist: Tawbah means deciding you are done, turning the ship around and planning to stay on course; nothing Allah granted us is more beautiful.

outline.heading: The man who found his lost camel
outline.gist: A man stranded in the desert lies in a grave he dug, then his camel returns with food and water; Allah is happier with your repentance than he was.

outline.heading: Hypocrites among the Bedouins and Medina
outline.gist: Some around Medina pledged allegiance only for protection and benefits like zakat.

outline.heading: Dead weight in a community
outline.gist: Hypocrites inflate the numbers but are absent when money, volunteers or experts are needed, then demand service and complain about the facility; the Prophet himself saw half his people stay back.

outline.heading: Always give more than you take
outline.gist: In communal work everyone must contribute more than they receive; only the youth may take more, so they can build their character before they give.

outline.heading: Our real problems are internal
outline.gist: Entrenched hypocrisy is punished twice because it rots the ummah from within; our defeats come from ourselves, not our enemies.

outline.heading: Those who admit their sins: that's us
outline.gist: Another group admits their sins and mixes good with bad, and Allah may forgive them; scholars wept and spent whole nights repeating this verse.

outline.heading: The deferred group: the indifferent
outline.gist: A third group neither repents nor commits; they drift through life and their judgment is left to Allah.

outline.heading: Find which group you are in
outline.gist: Do not be the professional hypocrite who avoids responsibility, nor the indifferent one gambling on the outcome; be among those who admit their faults and turn to Allah.

outline.heading: Admitting fault goes a long way
outline.gist: Being able to admit you were wrong matters with Allah just as it does in marriage and other relationships.

outline.heading: Tabuk: the hour of difficulty
outline.gist: Allah accepted the repentance of the Prophet and all who marched to Tabuk in heat, hunger and poverty, because everyone always needs tawbah.

outline.heading: The excuses of those who stayed behind
outline.gist: On the return most of those who stayed home came with excuses, some true and many false, and the Prophet prayed for their forgiveness.

outline.heading: Ka'b ibn Malik: no excuse at all
outline.gist: Three men stayed back with no excuse; one was Ka'b, a famous poet and an early Muslim who had been present at a decisive moment in Islam's history.

outline.heading: Ka'b chooses the truth
outline.gist: A gifted speaker who could talk his way out with anyone else, Ka'b told the Prophet the truth knowing revelation would expose a lie; honesty earns no medal, it is simply the only way to live.

outline.heading: Fifty days of boycott
outline.gist: Ka'b and the two others were shunned for fifty days, the length of the Tabuk expedition, with no one speaking or returning their salams.

outline.heading: The king's letter
outline.gist: A king invited Ka'b to his court; he wept that Allah's enemies now saw weakness in him, and burned the letter.

outline.heading: The day of acceptance
outline.gist: Everyone makes mistakes; on the fiftieth day the verses came, the Prophet called it the best day of Ka'b's life, and the Muslims embraced him.

outline.heading: No refuge from Allah except in Him
outline.gist: The vast earth felt narrow and their chests tight until they realised there is no running away from Allah, only running back to Him.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Tawbah needs acknowledgement, remorse and a plan; an apology is not enough for mocking the sacred, and Allah rejoices at a servant's return.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Those who admit mixed deeds are forgiven, and Ka'b's honest repentance shows the only refuge from Allah is in Him.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: Hypocrites fear exposure, mock the deen and call it a joke, and go along with religion only for social reasons.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: Entrenched hypocrites take benefits without contributing and rot the ummah from within.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Members who only take and complain are dead weight; everyone except the youth must give more than they take.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Work out which of the three groups you belong to, and learn to admit fault.

themes.label: Truthfulness and honesty
themes.note: Ka'b told the truth when lying seemed free, accepted the consequences, and stayed loyal under temptation.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: The story of Ka'b ibn Malik and the two others left behind from Tabuk.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Young people should walk away from friend groups that mock Allah and the Prophet.

hadith.gist: The door of repentance remains open until the sun rises from the west, and for each person until the soul leaves the body.
Allah is happier with His servant's repentance than a man stranded in the desert who finds his lost camel with its food and water, and in his joy says 'You are my servant and I am Your lord'.
Ka'b ibn Malik's own account of staying behind from Tabuk, telling the truth, the fifty-day boycott and the acceptance of his repentance.

maxims: Tawbah is the most beautiful thing in the universe
You always have to give more than you take
Our problems as a nation have always been internal
An apology won't cut it; you need repentance
No point running away from Allah; run back to Him
The hypocrite will expose himself eventually

stories.who: The man who lost his camel in the desert
stories.point: Allah's joy at a servant's repentance exceeds the joy of a man saved from death.

stories.who: Those who stayed behind from Tabuk
stories.point: Many escaped with false excuses in this world, but the consequences come later.

stories.who: Ka'b ibn Malik
stories.point: He refused to lie, bore fifty days of boycott, rejected a king's offer and was forgiven: honesty and running back to Allah.

contemporary: Relapse after addiction rehab when people lack remorse
Community members who demand services from the masjid but rarely volunteer or donate
takeaways: Make tawbah complete: admit the wrong, feel remorse, and remove at least one factor that makes the sin easy.
Walk away from groups that mock Allah, the Prophet or the deen, without starting a fight.
Pull your weight in the community and give more than you take.
Be among those who admit their sins and keep turning to Allah, and practise admitting fault in your relationships.
Tell the truth even when a lie seems to cost nothing.

7:85.ar: وَإِلَىٰ مَدۡيَنَ أَخَاهُمۡ شُعَيۡبࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥۖ قَدۡ جَآءَتۡكُم بَيِّنَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ فَأَوۡفُواْ ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ وَلَا تَبۡخَسُواْ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشۡيَآءَهُمۡ وَلَا تُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بَعۡدَ إِصۡلَٰحِهَاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
7:85.en: And unto Midian (We sent) their brother, Shu'eyb. He said: O my people! Serve Allah. Ye have no other Allah save Him. Lo! a clear proof hath come unto you from your Lord; so give full measure and full weight and wrong not mankind in their goods, and work not confusion in the earth after the fair ordering thereof. That will be better for you, if ye are believers

7:86.ar: وَلَا تَقۡعُدُواْ بِكُلِّ صِرَٰطࣲ تُوعِدُونَ وَتَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِهِۦ وَتَبۡغُونَهَا عِوَجࣰ اۚ وَٱذۡكُرُوٓاْ إِذۡ كُنتُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا فَكَثَّرَكُمۡۖ وَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
7:86.en: Lurk not on every road to threaten (wayfarers), and to turn away from Allah's path him who believeth in Him, and to seek to make it crooked. And remember, when ye were but few, how He did multiply you. And see the nature of the consequence for the corrupters

7:87.ar: وَإِن كَانَ طَآئِفَةࣱ مِّنكُمۡ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱلَّذِيٓ أُرۡسِلۡتُ بِهِۦ وَطَآئِفَةࣱ لَّمۡ يُؤۡمِنُواْ فَٱصۡبِرُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَحۡكُمَ ٱللَّهُ بَيۡنَنَاۚ وَهُوَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡحَٰكِمِينَ
7:87.en: And if there is a party of you which believeth in that wherewith I have been sent, and there is a party which believeth not, then have patience until Allah judge between us. He is the Best of all who deal in judgment

7:88.ar: ۞قَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ لَنُخۡرِجَنَّكَ يَٰشُعَيۡبُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَكَ مِن قَرۡيَتِنَآ أَوۡ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِي مِلَّتِنَاۚ قَالَ أَوَلَوۡ كُنَّا كَٰرِهِينَ
7:88.en: The chieftains of his people, who were scornful, said: Surely we will drive thee out, O Shu'eyb, and those who believe with thee, from our township, unless ye return to our religion. He said: Even though we hate it

7:89.ar: قَدِ ٱفۡتَرَيۡنَا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا إِنۡ عُدۡنَا فِي مِلَّتِكُم بَعۡدَ إِذۡ نَجَّىٰنَا ٱللَّهُ مِنۡهَاۚ وَمَا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّعُودَ فِيهَآ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّنَاۚ وَسِعَ رَبُّنَا كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ عِلۡمًاۚ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوَكَّلۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا ٱفۡتَحۡ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَ قَوۡمِنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡفَٰتِحِينَ
7:89.en: We should have invented a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah hath rescued us from it. It is not for us to return to it unless Allah our Lord should (so) will. Our Lord comprehendeth all things in knowledge. In Allah do we put our trust. Our Lord! Decide with truth between us and our folk, for Thou art the best of those who make decision

7:90.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ لَئِنِ ٱتَّبَعۡتُمۡ شُعَيۡبًا إِنَّكُمۡ إِذࣰ ا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
7:90.en: But the chieftains of his people, who were disbelieving, said: If ye follow Shu'eyb, then truly ye shall be the losers

7:91.ar: فَأَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلرَّجۡفَةُ فَأَصۡبَحُواْ فِي دَارِهِمۡ جَٰثِمِينَ
7:91.en: So the earthquake seized them and morning found them prostrate in their dwelling-place

7:92.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ شُعَيۡبࣰ ا كَأَن لَّمۡ يَغۡنَوۡاْ فِيهَاۚ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ شُعَيۡبࣰ ا كَانُواْ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
7:92.en: Those who denied Shu'eyb became as though they had not dwelt there. Those who denied Shu'eyb, they were the losers

7:93.ar: فَتَوَلَّىٰ عَنۡهُمۡ وَقَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ لَقَدۡ أَبۡلَغۡتُكُمۡ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّي وَنَصَحۡتُ لَكُمۡۖ فَكَيۡفَ ءَاسَىٰ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ كَٰفِرِينَ
7:93.en: So he turned from them and said: O my people! I delivered my Lord's messages unto you and gave you good advice; then how can I sorrow for a people that rejected (truth)

7:94.ar: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا فِي قَرۡيَةࣲ مِّن نَّبِيٍّ إِلَّآ أَخَذۡنَآ أَهۡلَهَا بِٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَضَّرَّعُونَ
7:94.en: And We sent no prophet unto any township but We did afflict its folk with tribulation and adversity that haply they might grow humble

7:95.ar: ثُمَّ بَدَّلۡنَا مَكَانَ ٱلسَّيِّئَةِ ٱلۡحَسَنَةَ حَتَّىٰ عَفَواْ وَّقَالُواْ قَدۡ مَسَّ ءَابَآءَنَا ٱلضَّرَّآءُ وَٱلسَّرَّآءُ فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُم بَغۡتَةࣰ وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
7:95.en: Then changed We the evil plight for good till they grew affluent and said: Tribulation and distress did touch our fathers. Then We seized them unawares, when they perceived not

7:96.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱتَّقَوۡاْ لَفَتَحۡنَا عَلَيۡهِم بَرَكَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبُواْ فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
7:96.en: And if the people of the townships had believed and kept from evil, surely We should have opened for them blessings from the sky and from the earth. But (unto every messenger) they gave the lie, and so We seized them on account of what they used to earn

7:97.ar: أَفَأَمِنَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُم بَأۡسُنَا بَيَٰتࣰ ا وَهُمۡ نَآئِمُونَ
7:97.en: Are the people of the townships then secure from the coming of Our wrath upon them as a night-raid while they sleep

7:98.ar: أَوَأَمِنَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُم بَأۡسُنَا ضُحࣰ ى وَهُمۡ يَلۡعَبُونَ
7:98.en: Or are the people of the townships then secure from the coming of Our wrath upon them in the daytime while they play

7:99.ar: أَفَأَمِنُواْ مَكۡرَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَلَا يَأۡمَنُ مَكۡرَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
7:99.en: Are they then secure from Allah's scheme? None deemeth himself secure from Allah's scheme save folk that perish

7:100.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَهۡدِ لِلَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَهۡلِهَآ أَن لَّوۡ نَشَآءُ أَصَبۡنَٰهُم بِذُنُوبِهِمۡۚ وَنَطۡبَعُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡمَعُونَ
7:100.en: Is it not an indication to those who inherit the land after its people (who thus reaped the consequence of evil-doing) that, if We will, We can smite them for their sins and print upon their hearts so that they hear not

7:101.ar: تِلۡكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآئِهَاۚ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ مِن قَبۡلُۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَطۡبَعُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
7:101.en: Such were the townships. We relate some tidings of them unto thee (Muhammad). Their messengers verily came unto them with clear proofs (of Allah's Sovereignty), but they could not believe because they had before denied. Thus doth Allah print upon the hearts of disbelievers (that they hear not)

7:102.ar: وَمَا وَجَدۡنَا لِأَكۡثَرِهِم مِّنۡ عَهۡدࣲۖ وَإِن وَجَدۡنَآ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَفَٰسِقِينَ
7:102.en: We found no (loyalty to any) covenant in most of them. Nay, most of them We found wrong-doers

7:103.ar: ثُمَّ بَعَثۡنَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِم مُّوسَىٰ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَإِيْهِۦ فَظَلَمُواْ بِهَاۖ فَٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
7:103.en: Then, after them, We sent Moses with our tokens unto Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they repelled them. Now, see the nature of the consequence for the corrupters

7:104.ar: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ يَٰفِرۡعَوۡنُ إِنِّي رَسُولࣱ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
7:104.en: Moses said: O Pharaoh! Lo! I am a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds

7:105.ar: حَقِيقٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَن لَّآ أَقُولَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَقَّۚ قَدۡ جِئۡتُكُم بِبَيِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ فَأَرۡسِلۡ مَعِيَ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ
7:105.en: Approved upon condition that I speak concerning Allah nothing but the truth. I come unto you (lords of Egypt) with a clear proof from your Lord. So let the Children of Israel go with me

7:106.ar: قَالَ إِن كُنتَ جِئۡتَ بِـَٔايَةࣲ فَأۡتِ بِهَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
7:106.en: (Pharaoh) said: If thou comest with a token, then produce it, if thou art of those who speak the truth

7:107.ar: فَأَلۡقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعۡبَانࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
7:107.en: Then he flung down his staff and lo! it was a serpent manifest

7:108.ar: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِيَ بَيۡضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ
7:108.en: And he drew forth his hand (from his bosom), and lo! it was white for the beholders

7:109.ar: قَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ مِن قَوۡمِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
7:109.en: The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said: Lo! this is some knowing wizard

7:110.ar: يُرِيدُ أَن يُخۡرِجَكُم مِّنۡ أَرۡضِكُمۡۖ فَمَاذَا تَأۡمُرُونَ
7:110.en: Who would expel you from your land. Now what do ye advise

7:111.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أَرۡجِهۡ وَأَخَاهُ وَأَرۡسِلۡ فِي ٱلۡمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ
7:111.en: They said (unto Pharaoh): Put him off (a while) - him and his brother - and send into the cities summoners

7:112.en: To bring each knowing wizard unto thee

7:113.ar: وَجَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ فِرۡعَوۡنَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجۡرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحۡنُ ٱلۡغَٰلِبِينَ
7:113.en: And the wizards came to Pharaoh, saying: Surely there will be a reward for us if we are victors

7:114.en: He answered: Yes, and surely ye shall be of those brought near (to me)

7:115.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلۡقِيَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ نَحۡنُ ٱلۡمُلۡقِينَ
7:115.en: They said: O Moses! Either throw (first) or let us be the first throwers

7:116.ar: قَالَ أَلۡقُواْۖ فَلَمَّآ أَلۡقَوۡاْ سَحَرُوٓاْ أَعۡيُنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱسۡتَرۡهَبُوهُمۡ وَجَآءُو بِسِحۡرٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
7:116.en: He said: Throw! And when they threw they cast a spell upon the people's eyes, and overawed them, and produced a mighty spell

7:117.ar: ۞وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنۡ أَلۡقِ عَصَاكَۖ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلۡقَفُ مَا يَأۡفِكُونَ
7:117.en: And We inspired Moses (saying): Throw thy staff! And lo! it swallowed up their lying show

7:118.ar: فَوَقَعَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَبَطَلَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
7:118.en: Thus was the Truth vindicated and that which they were doing was made vain

7:119.en: Thus were they there defeated and brought low

7:120.en: And the wizards fell down prostrate

7:121.en: Crying: We believe in the Lord of the Worlds

7:122.en: The Lord of Moses and Aaron

7:123.ar: قَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ ءَامَنتُم بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَنۡ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمۡۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَمَكۡرࣱ مَّكَرۡتُمُوهُ فِي ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ لِتُخۡرِجُواْ مِنۡهَآ أَهۡلَهَاۖ فَسَوۡفَ تَعۡلَمُونَ
7:123.en: Pharaoh said: Ye believe in Him before I give you leave! Lo! this is the plot that ye have plotted in the city that ye may drive its people hence. But ye shall come to know

7:124.ar: لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيۡدِيَكُمۡ وَأَرۡجُلَكُم مِّنۡ خِلَٰفࣲ ثُمَّ لَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
7:124.en: Surely I shall have your hands and feet cut off upon alternate sides. Then I shall crucify you every one

7:125.en: They said: Lo! We are about to return unto our Lord

7:126.ar: وَمَا تَنقِمُ مِنَّآ إِلَّآ أَنۡ ءَامَنَّا بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّنَا لَمَّا جَآءَتۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَآ أَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرࣰ ا وَتَوَفَّنَا مُسۡلِمِينَ
7:126.en: Thou takest vengeance on us only forasmuch as we believed the tokens of our Lord when they came unto us. Our Lord! Vouchsafe unto us steadfastness and make us die as men who have surrendered (unto Thee)

7:127.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ مِن قَوۡمِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ أَتَذَرُ مُوسَىٰ وَقَوۡمَهُۥ لِيُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَيَذَرَكَ وَءَالِهَتَكَۚ قَالَ سَنُقَتِّلُ أَبۡنَآءَهُمۡ وَنَسۡتَحۡيِۦ نِسَآءَهُمۡ وَإِنَّا فَوۡقَهُمۡ قَٰهِرُونَ
7:127.en: The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said: (O King), wilt thou suffer Moses and his people to make mischief in the land, and flout thee and thy gods? He said: We will slay their sons and spare their women, for lo! we are in power over them

7:128.ar: قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِ ٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱصۡبِرُوٓاْۖ إِنَّ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ لِلَّهِ يُورِثُهَا مَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦۖ وَٱلۡعَٰقِبَةُ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
7:128.en: And Moses said unto his people: Seek help in Allah and endure. Lo! the earth is Allah's. He giveth it for an inheritance to whom He will. And lo! the sequel is for those who keep their duty (unto Him)

7:129.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أُوذِينَا مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَأۡتِيَنَا وَمِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جِئۡتَنَاۚ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمۡ أَن يُهۡلِكَ عَدُوَّكُمۡ وَيَسۡتَخۡلِفَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرَ كَيۡفَ تَعۡمَلُونَ
7:129.en: They said: We suffered hurt before thou camest unto us, and since thou hast come unto us. He said: It may be that your Lord is going to destroy your adversary and make you viceroys in the earth, that He may see how ye behave

7:130.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَخَذۡنَآ ءَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِٱلسِّنِينَ وَنَقۡصࣲ مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَذَّكَّرُونَ
7:130.en: And we straitened Pharaoh's folk with famine and dearth of fruits, that peradventure they might heed

7:131.ar: فَإِذَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ قَالُواْ لَنَا هَٰذِهِۦۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَطَّيَّرُواْ بِمُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥٓۗ أَلَآ إِنَّمَا طَٰٓئِرُهُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:131.en: But whenever good befell them, they said: This is ours; and whenever evil smote them they ascribed it to the evil auspices of Moses and those with him. Surely their evil auspice was only with Allah. But most of them knew not

7:132.ar: وَقَالُواْ مَهۡمَا تَأۡتِنَا بِهِۦ مِنۡ ءَايَةࣲ لِّتَسۡحَرَنَا بِهَا فَمَا نَحۡنُ لَكَ بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
7:132.en: And they said: Whatever portent thou bringest wherewith to bewitch us, we shall not put faith in thee

7:133.ar: فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلطُّوفَانَ وَٱلۡجَرَادَ وَٱلۡقُمَّلَ وَٱلضَّفَادِعَ وَٱلدَّمَ ءَايَٰتࣲ مُّفَصَّلَٰتࣲ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ وَكَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا مُّجۡرِمِينَ
7:133.en: So We sent against them the flood and the locusts and the vermin and the frogs and the blood - a succession of clear signs. But they were arrogant and became a guilty folk

7:134.ar: وَلَمَّا وَقَعَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلرِّجۡزُ قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَى ٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَۖ لَئِن كَشَفۡتَ عَنَّا ٱلرِّجۡزَ لَنُؤۡمِنَنَّ لَكَ وَلَنُرۡسِلَنَّ مَعَكَ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ
7:134.en: And when the terror fell on them they cried: O Moses! Pray for us unto thy Lord, because He hath a covenant with thee. If thou removest the terror from us we verily will trust thee and will let the Children of Israel go with thee

7:135.ar: فَلَمَّا كَشَفۡنَا عَنۡهُمُ ٱلرِّجۡزَ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ هُم بَٰلِغُوهُ إِذَا هُمۡ يَنكُثُونَ
7:135.en: But when We did remove from them the terror for a term which they must reach, behold! they broke their covenant

7:136.ar: فَٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡ فَأَغۡرَقۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُواْ عَنۡهَا غَٰفِلِينَ
7:136.en: Therefore We took retribution from them; therefore We drowned them in the sea: because they denied Our revelations and were heedless of them

7:137.ar: وَأَوۡرَثۡنَا ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَانُواْ يُسۡتَضۡعَفُونَ مَشَٰرِقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَغَٰرِبَهَا ٱلَّتِي بَٰرَكۡنَا فِيهَاۖ وَتَمَّتۡ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُواْۖ وَدَمَّرۡنَا مَا كَانَ يَصۡنَعُ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَقَوۡمُهُۥ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡرِشُونَ
7:137.en: And We caused the folk who were despised to inherit the eastern parts of the land and the western parts thereof which We had blessed. And the fair word of thy Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their endurance; and We annihilated (all) that Pharaoh and his folk had done and that they had contrived

7:138.ar: وَجَٰوَزۡنَا بِبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَتَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ يَعۡكُفُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَصۡنَامࣲ لَّهُمۡۚ قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَى ٱجۡعَل لَّنَآ إِلَٰهࣰ ا كَمَا لَهُمۡ ءَالِهَةࣱۚ قَالَ إِنَّكُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ تَجۡهَلُونَ
7:138.en: And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came unto a people who were given up to idols which they had. They said: O Moses! Make for us a god even as they have gods. He said: Lo! ye are a folk who know not

7:139.ar: إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ مُتَبَّرࣱ مَّا هُمۡ فِيهِ وَبَٰطِلࣱ مَّا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
7:139.en: Lo! as for these, their way will be destroyed and all that they are doing is in vain

7:140.ar: قَالَ أَغَيۡرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبۡغِيكُمۡ إِلَٰهࣰ ا وَهُوَ فَضَّلَكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
7:140.en: He said: Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah when He hath favoured you above (all) creatures

7:141.ar: وَإِذۡ أَنجَيۡنَٰكُم مِّنۡ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ يَسُومُونَكُمۡ سُوٓءَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ يُقَتِّلُونَ أَبۡنَآءَكُمۡ وَيَسۡتَحۡيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمۡۚ وَفِي ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ عَظِيمࣱ‏
7:141.en: And (remember) when We did deliver you from Pharaoh's folk who were afflicting you with dreadful torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women. That was a tremendous trial from your Lord

7:142.ar: ۞وَوَٰعَدۡنَا مُوسَىٰ ثَلَٰثِينَ لَيۡلَةࣰ وَأَتۡمَمۡنَٰهَا بِعَشۡرࣲ فَتَمَّ مِيقَٰتُ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَرۡبَعِينَ لَيۡلَةࣰۚ وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَخِيهِ هَٰرُونَ ٱخۡلُفۡنِي فِي قَوۡمِي وَأَصۡلِحۡ وَلَا تَتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
7:142.en: And when We did appoint for Moses thirty nights (of solitude), and added to them ten, and he completed the whole time appointed by his Lord of forty nights; and Moses said unto his brother, Aaron: Take my place among the people. Do right, and follow not the way of mischief-makers

7:143.ar: وَلَمَّا جَآءَ مُوسَىٰ لِمِيقَٰتِنَا وَكَلَّمَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ قَالَ رَبِّ أَرِنِيٓ أَنظُرۡ إِلَيۡكَۚ قَالَ لَن تَرَىٰنِي وَلَٰكِنِ ٱنظُرۡ إِلَى ٱلۡجَبَلِ فَإِنِ ٱسۡتَقَرَّ مَكَانَهُۥ فَسَوۡفَ تَرَىٰنِيۚ فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُۥ لِلۡجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُۥ دَكࣰّ ا وَخَرَّ مُوسَىٰ صَعِقࣰ اۚ فَلَمَّآ أَفَاقَ قَالَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ تُبۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ وَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
7:143.en: And when Moses came to Our appointed tryst and his Lord had spoken unto him, he said: My Lord! Show me (Thy Self), that I may gaze upon Thee. He said: Thou wilt not see Me, but gaze upon the mountain! If it stand still in its place, then thou wilt see Me. And when his Lord revealed (His) glory to the mountain He sent it crashing down. And Moses fell down senseless. And when he woke he said: Glory unto Thee! I turn unto Thee repentant, and I am the first of (true) believers

7:144.ar: قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّي ٱصۡطَفَيۡتُكَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ بِرِسَٰلَٰتِي وَبِكَلَٰمِي فَخُذۡ مَآ ءَاتَيۡتُكَ وَكُن مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
7:144.en: He said: O Moses! I have preferred thee above mankind by My messages and by My speaking (unto thee). So hold that which I have given thee, and be among the thankful

7:145.ar: وَكَتَبۡنَا لَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأَلۡوَاحِ مِن كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ مَّوۡعِظَةࣰ وَتَفۡصِيلࣰ ا لِّكُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَخُذۡهَا بِقُوَّةࣲ وَأۡمُرۡ قَوۡمَكَ يَأۡخُذُواْ بِأَحۡسَنِهَاۚ سَأُوْرِيكُمۡ دَارَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
7:145.en: And We wrote for him, upon the tablets, the lesson to be drawn from all things and the explanation of all things, then (bade him): Hold it fast; and command thy people (saying): Take the better (course made clear) therein. I shall show thee the abode of evil-livers

7:65.ar: ۞وَإِلَىٰ عَادٍ أَخَاهُمۡ هُودࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥٓۚ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
7:65.en: And unto (the tribe of) A'ad (We sent) their brother, Hud. He said: O my people! Serve Allah. Ye have no other Allah save Him. Will ye not ward off (evil)

7:73.ar: وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمۡ صَٰلِحࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥۖ قَدۡ جَآءَتۡكُم بَيِّنَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ هَٰذِهِۦ نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمۡ ءَايَةࣰۖ فَذَرُوهَا تَأۡكُلۡ فِيٓ أَرۡضِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوٓءࣲ فَيَأۡخُذَكُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
7:73.en: And to (the tribe of) Thamud (We sent) their brother Salih. He said: O my people! Serve Allah. Ye have no other Allah save Him. A wonder from your Lord hath come unto you. Lo! this is the camel of Allah, a token unto you; so let her feed in Allah's earth, and touch her not with hurt lest painful torment seize you

7:148.ar: وَٱتَّخَذَ قَوۡمُ مُوسَىٰ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ مِنۡ حُلِيِّهِمۡ عِجۡلࣰ ا جَسَدࣰ ا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌۚ أَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّهُۥ لَا يُكَلِّمُهُمۡ وَلَا يَهۡدِيهِمۡ سَبِيلًاۘ ٱتَّخَذُوهُ وَكَانُواْ ظَٰلِمِينَ
7:148.en: And the folk of Moses, after (he left them), chose a calf (for worship), (made) out of their ornaments, of saffron hue, which gave a lowing sound. Saw they not that it spake not unto them nor guided them to any way? They chose it, and became wrong-doers

7:149.ar: وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فِيٓ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَرَأَوۡاْ أَنَّهُمۡ قَدۡ ضَلُّواْ قَالُواْ لَئِن لَّمۡ يَرۡحَمۡنَا رَبُّنَا وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
7:149.en: And when they feared the consequences thereof and saw that they had gone astray, they said: Unless our Lord have mercy on us and forgive us, we verily are of the lost

7:150.ar: وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ غَضۡبَٰنَ أَسِفࣰ ا قَالَ بِئۡسَمَا خَلَفۡتُمُونِي مِنۢ بَعۡدِيٓۖ أَعَجِلۡتُمۡ أَمۡرَ رَبِّكُمۡۖ وَأَلۡقَى ٱلۡأَلۡوَاحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأۡسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُۥٓ إِلَيۡهِۚ قَالَ ٱبۡنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱسۡتَضۡعَفُونِي وَكَادُواْ يَقۡتُلُونَنِي فَلَا تُشۡمِتۡ بِيَ ٱلۡأَعۡدَآءَ وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡنِي مَعَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
7:150.en: And when Moses returned unto his people, angry and grieved, he said: Evil is that (course) which ye took after I had left you. Would ye hasten on the judgment of your Lord? And he cast down the tablets, and he seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward him. He said: Son of my mother! Lo! the folk did judge me weak and almost killed me. Oh, make not mine enemies to triumph over me and place me not among the evil-doers

7:151.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ لِي وَلِأَخِي وَأَدۡخِلۡنَا فِي رَحۡمَتِكَۖ وَأَنتَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
7:151.en: He said: My Lord! Have mercy on me and on my brother; bring us into Thy mercy, Thou the Most Merciful of all who show mercy

7:152.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ ٱلۡعِجۡلَ سَيَنَالُهُمۡ غَضَبࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ وَذِلَّةࣱ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُفۡتَرِينَ
7:152.en: Lo! Those who chose the calf (for worship), terror from their Lord and humiliation will come upon them in the life of the world. Thus do We requite those who invent a lie

7:153.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ عَمِلُواْ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ ثُمَّ تَابُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهَا وَءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهَا لَغَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
7:153.en: But those who do ill-deeds and afterward repent and believe - lo! for them, afterward, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

7:154.ar: وَلَمَّا سَكَتَ عَن مُّوسَى ٱلۡغَضَبُ أَخَذَ ٱلۡأَلۡوَاحَۖ وَفِي نُسۡخَتِهَا هُدࣰ ى وَرَحۡمَةࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ هُمۡ لِرَبِّهِمۡ يَرۡهَبُونَ
7:154.en: Then, when the anger of Moses abated, he took up the tablets, and in their inscription there was guidance and mercy for all those who fear their Lord

7:155.ar: وَٱخۡتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوۡمَهُۥ سَبۡعِينَ رَجُلࣰ ا لِّمِيقَٰتِنَاۖ فَلَمَّآ أَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلرَّجۡفَةُ قَالَ رَبِّ لَوۡ شِئۡتَ أَهۡلَكۡتَهُم مِّن قَبۡلُ وَإِيَّٰيَۖ أَتُهۡلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَّآۖ إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتۡنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِهَا مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَهۡدِي مَن تَشَآءُۖ أَنتَ وَلِيُّنَا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَاۖ وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡغَٰفِرِينَ
7:155.en: And Moses chose of his people seventy men for Our appointed tryst and, when the trembling came on them, he said: My Lord! If Thou hadst willed Thou hadst destroyed them long before, and me with them. Wilt thou destroy us for that which the ignorant among us did? It is but Thy trial (of us). Thou sendest whom Thou wilt astray and guidest whom Thou wilt: Thou art our Protecting Friend, therefore forgive us and have mercy on us, Thou, the Best of all who show forgiveness

7:156.ar: ۞وَٱكۡتُبۡ لَنَا فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣰ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَۚ قَالَ عَذَابِيٓ أُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَنۡ أَشَآءُۖ وَرَحۡمَتِي وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ فَسَأَكۡتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:156.en: And ordain for us in this world that which is good, and in the Hereafter (that which is good), Lo! We have turned unto Thee. He said: I smite with My punishment whom I will, and My mercy embraceth all things, therefore I shall ordain it for those who ward off (evil) and pay the poor-due, and those who believe Our revelations

7:157.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِيَّ ٱلۡأُمِّيَّ ٱلَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُۥ مَكۡتُوبًا عِندَهُمۡ فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ يَأۡمُرُهُم بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡهَىٰهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡخَبَٰٓئِثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنۡهُمۡ إِصۡرَهُمۡ وَٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ ٱلَّتِي كَانَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِهِۦ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلنُّورَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ مَعَهُۥٓ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
7:157.en: Those who follow the messenger, the Prophet who can neither read nor write, whom they will find described in the Torah and the Gospel (which are) with them. He will enjoin on them that which is right and forbid them that which is wrong. He will make lawful for them all good things and prohibit for them only the foul; and he will relieve them of their burden and the fetters that they used to wear. Then those who believe in him, and honour him, and help him, and follow the light which is sent down with him: they are the successful

7:159.ar: وَمِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰٓ أُمَّةࣱ يَهۡدُونَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَبِهِۦ يَعۡدِلُونَ
7:159.en: And of Moses' folk there is a community who lead with truth and establish justice therewith

7:160.ar: وَقَطَّعۡنَٰهُمُ ٱثۡنَتَيۡ عَشۡرَةَ أَسۡبَاطًا أُمَمࣰ اۚ وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱسۡتَسۡقَىٰهُ قَوۡمُهُۥٓ أَنِ ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلۡحَجَرَۖ فَٱنۢبَجَسَتۡ مِنۡهُ ٱثۡنَتَا عَشۡرَةَ عَيۡنࣰ اۖ قَدۡ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسࣲ مَّشۡرَبَهُمۡۚ وَظَلَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡغَمَٰمَ وَأَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلۡوَىٰۖ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡۚ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
7:160.en: We divided them into twelve tribes, nations; and We inspired Moses, when his people asked him for water, saying: Smite with thy staff the rock! And there gushed forth therefrom twelve springs, so that each tribe knew their drinking-place. And we caused the white cloud to overshadow them and sent down for them the manna and the quails (saying): Eat of the good things wherewith we have provided you. They wronged Us not, but they were wont to wrong themselves

7:161.ar: وَإِذۡ قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱسۡكُنُواْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةَ وَكُلُواْ مِنۡهَا حَيۡثُ شِئۡتُمۡ وَقُولُواْ حِطَّةࣱ وَٱدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡبَابَ سُجَّدࣰ ا نَّغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِكُمۡۚ سَنَزِيدُ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
7:161.en: And when it was said unto them: Dwell in this township and eat therefrom whence ye will, and say "Repentance," and enter the gate prostrate; We shall forgive you your sins; We shall increase (reward) for the right-doers

7:162.ar: فَبَدَّلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ قَوۡلًا غَيۡرَ ٱلَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمۡ فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِجۡزࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَظۡلِمُونَ
7:162.en: But those of them who did wrong changed the word which had been told them for another saying, and We sent down upon them wrath from heaven for their wrongdoing

7:163.ar: وَسۡـَٔلۡهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ ٱلَّتِي كَانَتۡ حَاضِرَةَ ٱلۡبَحۡرِ إِذۡ يَعۡدُونَ فِي ٱلسَّبۡتِ إِذۡ تَأۡتِيهِمۡ حِيتَانُهُمۡ يَوۡمَ سَبۡتِهِمۡ شُرَّعࣰ ا وَيَوۡمَ لَا يَسۡبِتُونَ لَا تَأۡتِيهِمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَبۡلُوهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡسُقُونَ
7:163.en: Ask them (O Muhammad) of the township that was by the sea, how they did break the Sabbath, how their big fish came unto them visibly upon their Sabbath day and on a day when they did not keep Sabbath came they not unto them. Thus did We try them for that they were evil-livers

7:164.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَتۡ أُمَّةࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوۡمًا ٱللَّهُ مُهۡلِكُهُمۡ أَوۡ مُعَذِّبُهُمۡ عَذَابࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ اۖ قَالُواْ مَعۡذِرَةً إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ
7:164.en: And when a community among them said: Why preach ye to a folk whom Allah is about to destroy or punish with an awful doom, they said: In order to be free from guilt before your Lord, and that haply they may ward off (evil)

7:165.ar: فَلَمَّا نَسُواْ مَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهِۦٓ أَنجَيۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ يَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلسُّوٓءِ وَأَخَذۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ بِعَذَابِۭ بَـِٔيسِۭ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡسُقُونَ
7:165.en: And when they forgot that whereof they had been reminded, We rescued those who forbade wrong, and visited those who did wrong with dreadful punishment because they were evil-livers

7:166.ar: فَلَمَّا عَتَوۡاْ عَن مَّا نُهُواْ عَنۡهُ قُلۡنَا لَهُمۡ كُونُواْ قِرَدَةً خَٰسِـِٔينَ
7:166.en: So when they took pride in that which they had been forbidden, We said unto them: Be ye apes despised and loathed

7:168.ar: وَقَطَّعۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أُمَمࣰ اۖ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلصَّٰلِحُونَ وَمِنۡهُمۡ دُونَ ذَٰلِكَۖ وَبَلَوۡنَٰهُم بِٱلۡحَسَنَٰتِ وَٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
7:168.en: And We have sundered them in the earth as (separate) nations. Some of them are righteous, and some far from that. And We have tried them with good things and evil things that haply they might return

7:172.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَأَشۡهَدَهُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ أَلَسۡتُ بِرَبِّكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ شَهِدۡنَآۚ أَن تَقُولُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنۡ هَٰذَا غَٰفِلِينَ
7:172.en: And (remember) when thy Lord brought forth from the Children of Adam, from their reins, their seed, and made them testify of themselves, (saying): Am I not your Lord? They said: Yea, verily. We testify. (That was) lest ye should say at the Day of Resurrection: Lo! of this we were unaware

7:173.ar: أَوۡ تَقُولُوٓاْ إِنَّمَآ أَشۡرَكَ ءَابَآؤُنَا مِن قَبۡلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةࣰ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡۖ أَفَتُهۡلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلۡمُبۡطِلُونَ
7:173.en: Or lest ye should say: (It is) only (that) our fathers ascribed partners to Allah of old and we were (their) seed after them. Wilt Thou destroy us on account of that which those who follow falsehood did

7:175.ar: وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا فَٱنسَلَخَ مِنۡهَا فَأَتۡبَعَهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَاوِينَ
7:175.en: Recite unto them the tale of him to whom We gave Our revelations, but he sloughed them off, so Satan overtook him and he became of those who lead astray

7:176.ar: وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَرَفَعۡنَٰهُ بِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّهُۥٓ أَخۡلَدَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُۚ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡكَلۡبِ إِن تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡهِ يَلۡهَثۡ أَوۡ تَتۡرُكۡهُ يَلۡهَثۚ ذَّٰلِكَ مَثَلُ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَاۚ فَٱقۡصُصِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
7:176.en: And had We willed We could have raised him by their means, but he clung to the earth and followed his own lust. Therefor his likeness is as the likeness of a dog: if thou attackest him he panteth with his tongue out, and if thou leavest him he panteth with his tongue out. Such is the likeness of the people who deny Our revelations. Narrate unto them the history (of the men of old), that haply they may take thought

7:177.ar: سَآءَ مَثَلًا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَأَنفُسَهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَظۡلِمُونَ
7:177.en: Evil as an example are the folk who denied Our revelations, and were wont to wrong themselves

7:178.ar: مَن يَهۡدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدِيۖ وَمَن يُضۡلِلۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
7:178.en: He whom Allah leadeth, he indeed is led aright, while he whom Allah sendeth astray - they indeed are losers

7:180.ar: وَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ فَٱدۡعُوهُ بِهَاۖ وَذَرُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يُلۡحِدُونَ فِيٓ أَسۡمَٰٓئِهِۦۚ سَيُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
7:180.en: Allah's are the fairest names. Invoke Him by them. And leave the company of those who blaspheme His names. They will be requited what they do

7:187.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرۡسَىٰهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّيۖ لَا يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقۡتِهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ ثَقُلَتۡ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَا تَأۡتِيكُمۡ إِلَّا بَغۡتَةࣰۗ يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنۡهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:187.en: They ask thee of the (destined) Hour, when will it come to port. Say: Knowledge thereof is with my Lord only. He alone will manifest it at its proper time. It is heavy in the heavens and the earth. It cometh not to you save unawares. They question thee as if thou couldst be well informed thereof. Say: Knowledge thereof is with Allah only, but most of mankind know not

7:188.ar: قُل لَّآ أَمۡلِكُ لِنَفۡسِي نَفۡعࣰ ا وَلَا ضَرًّا إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَلَوۡ كُنتُ أَعۡلَمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ لَٱسۡتَكۡثَرۡتُ مِنَ ٱلۡخَيۡرِ وَمَا مَسَّنِيَ ٱلسُّوٓءُۚ إِنۡ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرࣱ وَبَشِيرࣱ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:188.en: Say: For myself I have no power to benefit, nor power to hurt, save that which Allah willeth. Had I knowledge of the Unseen, I should have abundance of wealth, and adversity would not touch me. I am but a warner, and a bearer of good tidings unto folk who believe

7:196.ar: إِنَّ وَلِـِّۧيَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي نَزَّلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَۖ وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
7:196.en: Lo! my Protecting Friend is Allah Who revealeth the Scripture. He befriendeth the righteous

7:197.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ نَصۡرَكُمۡ وَلَآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَنصُرُونَ
7:197.en: They on whom ye call beside Him have no power to help you, nor can they help you, nor can they help themselves

7:199.ar: خُذِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَ وَأۡمُرۡ بِٱلۡعُرۡفِ وَأَعۡرِضۡ عَنِ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
7:199.en: Keep to forgiveness (O Muhammad), and enjoin kindness, and turn away from the ignorant

7:200.ar: وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ نَزۡغࣱ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
7:200.en: And if a slander from the devil wound thee, then seek refuge in Allah. Lo! He is Hearer, Knower

7:201.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ إِذَا مَسَّهُمۡ طَٰٓئِفࣱ مِّنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ تَذَكَّرُواْ فَإِذَا هُم مُّبۡصِرُونَ
7:201.en: Lo! those who ward off (evil), when a glamour from the devil troubleth them, they do but remember (Allah's Guidance) and behold them seers

7:204.ar: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ فَٱسۡتَمِعُواْ لَهُۥ وَأَنصِتُواْ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
7:204.en: And when the Qur'an is recited, give ear to it and pay heed, that ye may obtain mercy

7:205.ar: وَٱذۡكُر رَّبَّكَ فِي نَفۡسِكَ تَضَرُّعࣰ ا وَخِيفَةࣰ وَدُونَ ٱلۡجَهۡرِ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ بِٱلۡغُدُوِّ وَٱلۡأٓصَالِ وَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡغَٰفِلِينَ
7:205.en: And do thou (O Muhammad) remember thy Lord within thyself humbly and with awe, below thy breath, at morn and evening. And be not thou of the neglectful

7:206.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ عَنۡ عِبَادَتِهِۦ وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُۥ وَلَهُۥ يَسۡجُدُونَۤ۩
7:206.en: Lo! those who are with thy Lord are not too proud to do Him service, but they praise Him and prostrate before Him

3:152.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُۥٓ إِذۡ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذۡنِهِۦۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلۡتُمۡ وَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَعَصَيۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَۚ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمۡ عَنۡهُمۡ لِيَبۡتَلِيَكُمۡۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا عَنكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
3:152.en: Allah verily made good His promise unto you when ye routed them by His leave, until (the moment) when your courage failed you, and ye disagreed about the order and ye disobeyed, after He had shown you that for which ye long. Some of you desired the world, and some of you desired the Hereafter. Therefore He made you flee from them, that He might try you. Yet now He hath forgiven you. Allah is a Lord of Kindness to believers

6:103.ar: لَّا تُدۡرِكُهُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدۡرِكُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَۖ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
6:103.en: Vision comprehendeth Him not, but He comprehendeth (all) vision. He is the Subtile, the Aware

14:48.ar: يَوۡمَ تُبَدَّلُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُۖ وَبَرَزُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡوَٰحِدِ ٱلۡقَهَّارِ
14:48.en: On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens (also will be changed) and they will come forth unto Allah, the One, the Almighty

ArZAqC5ylbU.speaker: adnan
ArZAqC5ylbU.speaker_note: hosts his own A Juz A Day Ramadan series; single voice throughout
ArZAqC5ylbU.title: A Juz A Day: 9th Juz, Musa vs Pharaoh
ArZAqC5ylbU.one_line: Surah Al-A'raf from Shuayb to the end: Musa against Pharaoh, the Israelites' lapses, the Sabbath-breakers and their preachers, and the primordial covenant.
ArZAqC5ylbU.summary: He reads the ninth juz as the second half of Surah Al-A'raf. Shuayb begins with tawhid but also confronts his people's financial corruption, which shows that believers must lead on society's moral problems, and calling him their brother shows that dawah starts from shared humanity, a lesson for Muslims in a non-Muslim country. Allah sends hardship to break arrogance, and those who stay arrogant are given prosperity before a harsher punishment; breaking commitments marks the evil. In the Musa narrative, the sorcerers recognize a real miracle and fall into prostration, holding firm under Pharaoh's threats, an example of courage born of iman and help from unexpected places. Pharaoh's people break their promise after every plague. He notes that the Quran praises the Israelites when they are patient and criticizes even the Companions when they err, a balance critics ignore. He discusses Musa's request to see Allah out of love, the calf, accountability starting at the top, and Allah's mercy that keeps offering chances. The Sabbath preachers model all advocacy: speak so you are excused before Allah and because someone may listen. The covenant of souls grounds the fitrah, and disbelief is its suppression. He closes with dua by Allah's names, forgiveness, commanding good and remembering Allah.

outline.heading: Opening
Shuayb's call to Midian
outline.gist: Worship Allah alone, give full measure, do not cheat people or spread corruption, and do not block the path of believers.

outline.heading: Threatened with expulsion, Shuayb refuses to return
outline.gist: Returning to their religion after Allah saved them would make them liars about their faith and about their principles; they put their trust in Allah and ask Him to judge.

outline.heading: The earthquake and Shuayb's farewell
outline.gist: The deniers are destroyed as if they never lived there, and Shuayb turns away having delivered his message and sincere advice.

outline.heading: Faith must address society's moral problems
outline.gist: Shuayb's people were financially exploitative; prophets addressed the specific moral rot of their society, and believers should lead on any oppression or unethical practice that affects everyone.

outline.heading: 'Their brother': dawah from shared humanity
outline.gist: Each prophet is called the brother of his people; dawah should start from shared identity and humanity rather than hostility, especially for Muslims in a non-Muslim majority country.

outline.heading: Hardship to humble, then prosperity before ruin
outline.gist: Before destroying a nation Allah sent hardship to break its arrogance; those who stayed arrogant were given prosperity, and their punishment then was fully deserved, a warning to Quraysh.

outline.heading: Do they feel safe from Allah's plan?
outline.gist: Had they believed they would have received blessings; the warnings about punishment by night or at play are meant to make us reprioritize, since individuals can still be punished to bring them back.

outline.heading: Most of them did not honour their commitments
outline.gist: Keeping promises separates good from evil people; someone who cannot be trusted with a promise cannot be trusted with iman and salvation.

outline.heading: Musa before Pharaoh: the staff and the hand
outline.gist: Musa declares his message and asks for the Israelites' release, showing the staff turning to a snake and his hand shining white.

outline.heading: Pharaoh gathers the sorcerers
outline.gist: The court calls Musa a sorcerer; the best magicians are summoned and ask for a reward; their spell petrifies the crowd and Musa feels natural fear.

outline.heading: The staff devours their tricks and the sorcerers fall prostrate
outline.gist: Experts in illusion recognize a real miracle and are thrown into prostration, believing in the Lord of Musa and Harun.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's threat and the sorcerers' steadfastness
outline.gist: Pharaoh brands them a national security threat and threatens crucifixion; they answer that their only crime is belief and ask Allah for patience and to die as Muslims.

outline.heading: Help from unexpected places and the courage of iman
outline.gist: Allah sends a prophet helpers from among his enemies, as He kept sending help to the Prophet in Makkah; courage that ignores consequences validates iman.

outline.heading: The earth belongs to Allah; the end belongs to the righteous
outline.gist: Rule of the earth is not a sign of goodness; Allah gives it as He wills, but the Hereafter is exclusively for the righteous, so seek help and stay steadfast.

outline.heading: Do not give up hope
outline.gist: The Israelites complain they are always persecuted; Musa tells them Allah may make them successors to see how they act.

outline.heading: Drought and plagues met with arrogance
outline.gist: Pharaoh's people credit themselves for good and blame Musa's omen for bad; the flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood only harden them.

outline.heading: A broken promise after every plague
outline.gist: Each time they beg Musa to pray for relief and promise to release the Israelites, then break the pledge, showing they are people of no principle.

outline.heading: Pharaoh drowned, the oppressed inherit the land
outline.gist: The brutally oppressed are made to rule the blessed land, east and west.

outline.heading: The Quran's balance: praise where due, blame where due
outline.gist: Allah credits the Israelites' patience and blames the Companions' mistakes at Uhud explicitly; critics who call the Quran hateful ignore this balance.

outline.heading: 'Make us a god like theirs'
outline.gist: Freshly saved from Pharaoh, the Israelites ask for an idol; Musa calls them foolish and reminds them of Allah's favour.

outline.heading: The forty nights and Harun as deputy
outline.gist: Musa's appointment grows from thirty to forty nights, and he leaves Harun in charge with instructions to keep order.

outline.heading: Musa asks to see Allah out of love
outline.gist: The request came not from doubt but from love and longing in one whom Allah spoke to directly.

outline.heading: The mountain crumbles; believers will see Allah later
outline.gist: No one can bear seeing Allah in this world; a glimpse turned a mountain to dust, but in the Hereafter, when the laws of this world end, the believers will see their Lord.

outline.heading: Musa repents and is reassured
outline.gist: Recognizing the request was not ideal, Musa repents at once; Allah reassures him he is chosen and tells him to hold firm and be grateful.

outline.heading: The tablets
outline.gist: Musa receives the tablets explaining everything, the revelation for his people.

outline.heading: The lowing calf that cannot guide
outline.gist: In his absence they worship a calf of jewellery that only makes a sound; idols cannot speak or guide, while Allah guides through revelation, reason and inspiration of the heart.

outline.heading: Musa's anger: accountability starts at the top
outline.gist: He seizes Harun, the one in charge, first; Harun explains they nearly killed him, and Musa prays for forgiveness for both.

outline.heading: The calf-worshippers' repentance and our easier tawbah
outline.gist: Their repentance required their lives because the stakes were so high; ours is words, resolve and remorse.

outline.heading: Guidance and mercy on the tablets; the seventy
outline.gist: All revelation carries guidance and mercy; the chosen seventy ask for something egregious, are punished and revived.

outline.heading: My mercy encompasses all things
outline.gist: Despite repeated failures the Israelites kept receiving prophets and chances; Allah keeps giving us chances and sends difficulty to humble us back to Him.

outline.heading: The unlettered Prophet who lifts burdens
outline.gist: He is described in the Torah and Gospel as bringing an easy law that removes the shackles of a hard one.

outline.heading: Not all alike: the twelve springs, cloud shade, manna and quails
outline.gist: The Quran praises a righteous group among them and recounts how Allah provided for the twelve tribes; when they complained, they wronged only themselves.

outline.heading: The Sabbath-breakers' loophole
outline.gist: Fish came only on the Sabbath, so they set rigs on Friday and collected on Sunday, trying to cut corners without openly breaking the law.

outline.heading: Why the preachers kept preaching
outline.gist: Told they were wasting their time, the preachers answered: to be excused before Allah, and because someone might listen; those who forbade evil were saved.

outline.heading: The basis of all activism and advocacy
outline.gist: Writing to MPs or speaking up is done so we can say we tried and because pressure can work; stay proactive and leave results to Allah.

outline.heading: Dispersed and tested with good and bad
outline.gist: The Israelites were scattered, some righteous, and tested with blessings and misfortune so they would return.

outline.heading: The covenant: 'Am I not your Lord?'
outline.gist: Allah drew out the offspring of Adam and made them testify, removing the excuse of blaming forefathers on Judgment Day.

outline.heading: The soul's pledge as the root of fitrah and morality
outline.gist: Souls existed before bodies and all took the pledge; its remnant drives the search for purpose and is the basis of ethics.

outline.heading: Kufr as suppression of the fitrah
outline.gist: Living without purpose requires suppressing the innate search for Allah; that suppression is disbelief, and every sane adult is accountable to their fitrah, with Allah judging what message reached them.

outline.heading: The man who cast off the signs: salvation is not guaranteed
outline.gist: Being born Muslim does not make salvation a done deal; it must be worked for every day.

outline.heading: Call on Allah by His beautiful names
outline.gist: Match the name to the need in dua: the Powerful for strength, the Provider for provision, the Forgiving for forgiveness, the Bestower for a child.

outline.heading: The Hour and the Prophet's human role
outline.gist: Only Allah knows the Hour; the Prophet has no power over benefit or harm and no knowledge of the unseen except what Allah grants; he is a warner and bearer of good news.

outline.heading: Only Allah protects
outline.gist: Those called on besides Him cannot even help themselves, so dua and worship are for Allah alone.

outline.heading: Forgive, command the good, turn from the ignorant
outline.gist: Three pillars of Islamic ethics: habitual pardoning and gentleness, working for justice in society, and knowledge that lets you stay gracious with provocateurs.

outline.heading: When Satan prompts, remember and see clearly
outline.gist: Believers slip, but the mindful remember Allah at once, seek forgiveness and set things right.

outline.heading: Listen to the Quran and remember Allah morning and evening
outline.gist: Quiet, humble, private remembrance as the Prophet practised it reconnects us when we stray.

outline.heading: The first prostration of the Quran
outline.gist: Those near Allah are not too proud to worship Him; the surah ends with the first sajdah in the mushaf.

outline.heading: Outro

Vision cannot grasp Him, explaining why Musa could not see Allah in this world
The earth and skies will be changed, so the limits that prevent seeing Allah end in the Hereafter

Accountability is top down
So we can tell Allah we did something, and maybe someone listens
